profile_id.description: `customer_profiles.id` — the CUSTOMER, not the Atribu profile. Named this way by the underlying scan and kept verbatim rather than renamed in one of three places.

suggested_email.description: What a backfill would write — recovered from identifiers or CRM raw data.

social_only_identifiers.description: Non-empty only for a "ghost": no email AND no phone, reachable only through a messaging surface (`instagram`, `manychat`, `whatsapp`).

profile_id.description: The customer being CHANGED — for a merge, the one merged away.

will_apply.description: False when the operation is a no-op or no longer valid; `reason` says which.

IdentityRepairApply.description: A partial success is the NORMAL outcome, not an error: an operation whose precondition moved since the preview lands in `skipped` with the reason, and the rest still apply. That is what makes the whole call safe to retry.

IdentityRepairOperation.description: One repair. There is NO actor field: the merge audit row records who did it, and that comes from the authenticated principal (a session's user, or null for an API key). Accepting it in the body would let any caller write any user's id into the audit log.

audit_log_id.description: Identifies the MERGE, not the customer. It is what an undo is keyed on.

merged_by_user_id.description: Who merged, or null for an automated repair.

is_currently_merged.description: False once the merge was undone. The row stays as the audit record.

merged_profile_id.description: The customer that has been restored as a separate person.

unmerge_audit_log_id.description: The audit row the UNDO itself wrote. The original merge's row stays as the record.

lead_restored.description: True when the merged customer's `lead_created` event was put back — the mirror of `lead_coalesce` on the preview.

recompute_enqueued.description: Whether the re-attribution this undo requires reached the queue. False is reported, never fatal: the unmerge has already committed and the hourly staleness sweep will pick it up.

method.description: How the link was made: `payer_name_booking` | `skool_dm_link` (inferred), `booking_slot` | `dm_contact` | `payer_email` (deterministic). An open catalog — read it as a string.

confidence.description: The METHOD's confidence, never chosen by whoever recorded the link. `deterministic` rests on a shared identifier (an email, a phone, the same booking slot); `inferred` on a unique match of weaker facts (the same name plus a booked call, the same Instagram name plus a Skool link) and is labelled «inferido» wherever it carries credit.

status.description: `pending` — applied (it already carries credit) and awaiting review. `accepted` — kept, off the review list. `rejected` — its credit was removed; recording the same link again never revives it.

origin_event_at.description: When the origin's event happened: the booked call, the Skool link sent in the DM.

subject_event_at.description: When the subject's event happened: the payment, the Skool sign-up.

evidence.description: The facts the method matched on. Never a name, email or phone.

allOf.description: The person who carries the ad origin — the one who booked the call, the DM sender.

IdentityLink.description: A non-destructive link between two customers of this profile: the conversions of `subject` may inherit the ad origin of `origin`. Nothing is merged — both customers keep their own events, identifiers and conversions — so rejecting the link removes exactly the credit it gave.

IdentityLinkPerson.description: The person whose conversions gain the origin — the payer, the sign-up.

cash_value.description: Reporting-currency cash of the subject's conversions this link currently credits. Null when it carries no cash — not yet recomputed, or a link that only reaches a lead.

recompute_enqueued.description: Whether an attribution recompute was enqueued: on a reject, or on accepting a link that had been rejected — the two decisions that move credit.

provider.description: null for a product not synced from a store.

active.description: `false` for a product the store deactivated or deleted. Deactivated products ARE returned: a mirror has to learn about the removal, and omitting them makes a deleted product indistinguishable from one that simply stopped changing.

updated_at.description: When Atribu last wrote this row — the `updated_since` clock and the first half of the keyset cursor. Not the store's own timestamp; see `external_updated_at`.

variant_id.description: Atribu's own id, stable across syncs.

price.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

currency.description: ISO-4217. `null` on rows synced before the catalogue sync began capturing the shop's currency — reported as unknown rather than defaulted, because a price with the wrong unit is worse than a price with none.

inventory_quantity.description: Units available across every location; null when untracked.

inventory_state.description: The stock band Atribu derives. `low_stock` is Atribu's threshold (5 or fewer available), not something the store reports; `discontinued` means the product left ACTIVE status or was deleted. `null` means the band is unknown — which is what an UNTRACKED item is, and is not the same as `in_stock`.

inventory_policy.description: The store's oversell policy, verbatim (Shopify: DENY/CONTINUE).

updated_at.description: When Atribu last wrote this row.

order_ref.description: The number the shopper sees on their confirmation, where the store sent one. Frequently null — it reaches Atribu on the order-created webhook and never on a bulk re-sync.

status.description: Atribu's single answer to 'where is my order'. Coarser than the store's own two status fields, which are carried alongside unmodified. `delivered` outranks `fulfilled`: a store leaves `fulfillment_status` at `fulfilled` after delivery.

value_amount.description: The captured total where there is one, else the ordered total.

description.description: As the store stores it — HTML.

status.description: active | archived | draft

updated_at.description: Shopify's own last-modified time — the clock `updated_since` filters on.

variants.description: EVERY variant: a product with more than one page of variants is read to the end.

variant_id.description: Shopify's numeric variant id — the id a cart permalink takes.

options.description: The variant's option values (e.g. Talla: M), in store order.

price.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

compare_at_price.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

inventory_quantity.description: Units available across every location, as Shopify reports it now.

financial_status.description: Shopify's REST spelling — the same values the `orders/*` webhooks carry.

fulfillment_status.description: REST spelling; null while nothing is fulfilled.

phone.description: The order's phone, else the customer's, else the shipping, else the billing address's.

attributes.description: The order's custom (cart / note) attributes as a map — e.g. the `vitrina_order` a cart permalink carried.

total_price.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

lines.description: EVERY line item, read to the end.

external_user_id.description: The phone number (WhatsApp), IGSID (Instagram) or Gmail thread id (email).

linked_customer_is_payer.description: True when the linked customer is a real payer — has an email/phone or a cash conversion — as opposed to a thin DM-only profile.

enrichment_unavailable.description:
#1550 — Atribu's analytics store could not be read for this page, so the three fields it feeds hold their absent-evidence value rather than a measurement: `ad_name` and `campaign_name` are null, and `linked_customer_is_payer` was decided on the contact's own email/phone alone, without consulting cash conversions.

Everything else on the row — the conversation, its counts, its last message, its contact and every `referral_*` field — comes from Atribu's messaging core and is unaffected. `false` on every row of a healthy response.

is_inferred_source.description: True when Stage 5c inferred this ad as the conversation's likely source (`attribution_mode = native_conversation_model`). Decision-support only, never a deterministic claim.

value.description: The email, or the phone in E.164.

source.description: `chat` — the customer typed it in this conversation; `customer` — the value the linked customer already holds, listed only when a typed value differs from it.

detected_at.description: When the typed value was first detected. Null on a `customer` row.

is_new.description: A typed value that differs from the one the linked customer already holds.

amount.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

id.description: The `handoff_id` the minting call returned. Not the handle the URL carries — that is the human's capability, this is the agent's.

kind.description: What the human is being asked to do. `connect` an OAuth consent, `pick` a choice among the assets a consent exposed, `sign_dpa` a Data Processing Addendum, `checkout` a plan payment, `approve` a consequential write you asked to make.

status.description: `pending` until the human finishes, then terminal. `expired` is DERIVED at read time from `expires_at` — polling an expired hand-off answers 200 with this status, never 404, so you can tell 'mint a fresh one' from 'wrong id'.

url.description: The URL to hand to the human. Present ONLY while `status` is `pending`; null once the hand-off is terminal, because a spent capability is not handed back out. The page is session-less — whoever holds this link can complete it, signed in or not, on a phone.

start_url.description: `connect` hand-offs only (#1800): the provider's own consent start, which redirects STRAIGHT to the provider's consent screen with no page in between. Send a partner app's user here; `url` is the fallback for a human with no app behind them. Same capability and same lifetime as `url` — present only while `status` is `pending`, dead the moment the hand-off settles, and null for every other kind.

expires_at.description: When the URL stops working. 45 minutes from the mint unless the kind says otherwise — the same budget Atribu's consumer connect detour ships against.

completed_at.description: When the hand-off settled, in any terminal status. Null while pending.

result.description: Kind-specific output, written when the hand-off settles. Carries `completed_by` (the Atribu user id) when a signed-in person finished it, and null there when an anonymous link holder did. Null while pending.

PendingAction.description: One hand-off: a step of the golden path only a human can take. Mint it through the route for its kind, hand `url` over, poll this endpoint until `status` is no longer `pending`, then continue.

status.description: `not_connected`: no live connection for this provider on the profile. `reconnect_required`: a connection needs re-authorization — its last-synced stages are still listed and their mappings still editable, but offer the reconnect first. `awaiting_sync`: connected, but Atribu has not read its pipelines yet. `ready`: `stages` lists every stage. Whatever is not `ready` comes with a `next_step`.

synced_at.description: When the pipelines were last read from the CRM.

can_write.description: Whether this credential can write the mapping: it holds `goals:write` and the profile has the `atribu_attribution` entitlement. `false` ⇒ every PATCH would be refused.

write_blocked_reason.description: Why `can_write` is false, one value per fix: `insufficient_scope` (re-mint the key under the `attribution` grant) or `entitlement_required` (the app enables `PUT /api/v1/profiles/{profileId}/entitlements/atribu_attribution`). `null` when writable.

body.description: JSON body to send, or `null` for none (the hand-off takes an optional one).

next_step.description: The call that moves the sheet forward, with the same credential: `sync_pipelines` (`POST /api/v1/connections/sync {provider:"gohighlevel", resource:"pipelines"}`, then poll `GET /api/v1/connections/sync/status?provider=gohighlevel` and read this again), `reconnect` / `connect` (`POST /api/v1/connections/gohighlevel/handoff`). `null` when `ready` and every stage is stored.

outcomes.description: Every outcome a stage can map to, in picker order, with its label in `locale`.

stages.description: Every stage of every pipeline of every connected location, in CRM order.

position.description: The stage's position in its pipeline (CRM order).

connection_id.description: The connection the stage was read through.

suggested.description: What Atribu suggests this stage means, from its name. Deterministic (no model call): the same stage name always gets the same suggestion. `null` when the name does not point to an outcome — `no_suggestion_reason` says why.

no_suggestion_label.description: `no_suggestion_reason` as a sentence in the requested `locale`, ready to show.

outcome.description: The mapped outcome key: one of `outcomes[].key`, or `unmapped` — a stage Atribu found with no suggestion; it counts as NO outcome (no conversion, no attribution) until someone maps it. `unmapped` is never written by a caller (pick an outcome or `ignored`).

source.description: Where the mapping came from. `unmapped` is always `engine_default`. Otherwise this is BEST-EFFORT, derived from the row: `suggested` = it equals the suggestion; `user` = it differs and the row was updated after Atribu created it; `engine_default` = it differs and was never updated (an older silent default nobody chose — treat it as unset). Known misreads: an engine-side rename of the stage makes an untouched row read `user`, and a mapping saved by a full-family replace reads `engine_default`. Before overwriting a `user` row, ask.

current.description: The mapping in force — what ingestion uses today. `null` until the stage is stored.

outcome_definition_id.description: The row `PATCH /api/v1/outcome-definitions/{id}` writes. `null` until Atribu has stored the stage (the next pipelines sync after the CRM connects, or after a stage is added).

writable.description: Whether THIS credential can write this row now.

not_writable_reason.description: `awaiting_sync`: Atribu has not stored the stage yet (see `next_step`). `insufficient_scope`: the credential lacks `goals:write`. `entitlement_required`: it has `goals:write` but the profile lacks the `atribu_attribution` entitlement (the PATCH answers 409).

not_writable_label.description: `not_writable_reason` as a sentence in the requested `locale`, ready to show.

document.description: Which agreement was accepted. `dpa` writes only the DPA columns; `baa` is the combined DPA & BAA click-wrap that Healthcare Mode requires and writes both.

document_version.description: The version stamp actually recorded — one of the shipped texts, never the raw string a caller sent.

already_accepted.description: True when this document was ALREADY accepted and nothing was written — the call is idempotent at the document grain, so a reload never collects a second signature and never moves the original timestamp.

document_version.description: Which shipped text you displayed. Allowlisted — an unknown value is a 422. Omit to accept the document's current version.

plan.description: The plan to buy. Free has nothing to sell and Enterprise is negotiated, so neither is accepted here — `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/subscription`'s `upgrade_available` lists exactly what this workspace can be sold.

interval.description: Billing cadence. Defaults to `monthly` — an agent asking for "the Growth plan" has expressed a complete intent, and requiring a cadence would turn a one-argument hand-off into a two-argument one for no gain.

webhook_url.description: The URL the merchant pastes into Shopify admin → Settings → Notifications → Webhooks. It carries the connection's inbound token, which routes the delivery; the delivery is only TRUSTED after its HMAC verifies against the signing ID below.

topics.description: The webhook topics to create. Deliberately narrower than the App Store install's set: every other topic needs the Admin API, which a manual connection has no token for, so advertising them would ask the merchant to queue work that can only fail.

state.description:
`pending` — created, no verified delivery has ever arrived. `connected` — a delivery verified inside the staleness window. `stale` — deliveries arrived once and stopped, which is the ONLY signal available: Shopify deletes a failing admin-created webhook and emails the store owner, not us.

Derived from `last_delivery_at`, never stored — `connection_status` has no such members.

last_processing_error_at.description: A delivery that verified and then threw while being processed. This route answers 200 to those (a 5xx would walk Shopify toward deleting the subscription), so without this field the dropped order is invisible in both directions.

signing_id_configured.description: Whether a signing ID has been stored. **The value is never returned.** It lives inside the sealed credentials envelope and leaves this API in no response, on any route — set it with the PATCH below, and if it is lost, set a new one.

shop_domain.description: The store handle, `<handle>.myshopify.com`, or a pasted admin URL — all three normalise. A custom storefront domain is REFUSED: Shopify always sends the `.myshopify.com` form on `X-Shopify-Shop-Domain`, so a stored custom domain could never be cross-checked against a delivery.

plan.description: `free` provisions the $0 tier here. `growth`/`agency` both hand back the same Shopify plan page — see above.

profile_id.description: Where to land the merchant after a `free` selection. A BODY field rather than the request's scope: this route reads and writes the WORKSPACE, and the profile only names a destination.

value.description: Normalised: lowercased, with a leading `@` or `#` stripped.

media_count.description:
Distinct media captured on this source's most recent snapshot day.

**`null` is not zero.** The count is a paged read of a snapshot-shaped table; when it cannot be assembled the field is `null` so a stalled sync is distinguishable from a handle that has never returned a post. Rendering it as `0` is exactly the bug #748 fixed.

id.description: `instagram_accounts.id` — the BINDING, not the Instagram account itself.

provider_subtype.description: `fb_login` (through a Facebook Page) or `ig_login` (Instagram Business Login). They differ in which id sends a DM and which scopes the grant carries.

comment_to_dm_paused_until.description: Set while the comment-to-DM circuit breaker is tripped. Clear it with `POST /api/v1/instagram/accounts/{account_id}/resume-comment-to-dm`.

is_automation_owner.description: One IG account can be connected from several workspaces; exactly one binding runs its automations. Disconnecting the owner promotes a surviving binding.

connection_status.description: From `data_connections`; `unknown` when that row could not be read.

post_id_allowlist.description: Media ids this trigger is restricted to; `null` means every post.

opening_message.description: The DM sent when the trigger fires.

public_comment_reply.description: Optional public reply left on the comment itself.

exact_dm_ad_count.description: Attributed to an ad by an exact DM referral — deterministic.

exact_follow_proxy_count.description: Attributed through a Follow Proxy click — deterministic.

avg_modeled_confidence.description: Mean 0–1 confidence of the MODELED credit; null when nothing was modeled.

mapped_in_manychat.description: False means this ad's conversations cannot be attributed deterministically — it is what makes the list actionable.

expected_followers.description: The SUM of per-event probabilities, not a count — a fractional value is correct.

evidence.description: The extractor's raw evidence blob — opaque, for display only.

widget_token.description: One-shot token for Fintoc's own widget.

stage_mapping_provider.description: `gemini` when the AI-assisted pass ran and returned at least one mapping, `rules` otherwise (AI unconfigured, the workspace's daily allowance is spent, or the model call failed — every case degrades to the rule-based suggestions, never an error).

stage_mapping_model.description: The model id that produced the AI-assisted mappings, or null on `rules`.

gemini_mappings_applied.description: How many stages took the AI suggestion over the rule-based one.

instagram_accounts.description: The profile's Instagram accounts — the candidates for the binding.

top_rejection_reason.description: Most frequent rejection in the window: `instagram_account_not_bound`, `invalid_payload`, `invalid_json` or `conversation_upsert_failed`.

events.description: What the event endpoint did with this connection's events. `null` when the read failed.

dry_run.description: A test event: shown here, never counted in `events`.

recent_events.description: The latest events the endpoint logged for this connection (newest first, at most 10). Metadata only.

flow_id.description: A ManyChat flow id, matched against an event's `flow_id`. Set this OR `keyword`.

keyword.description: An automation keyword / ice breaker, matched (case-insensitive) against `selected_intent` and `ad_ref`.

ManyChatFlowMappingEntry.description: One key → one ad. A key naming several ads is several rows. A match is MODELED attribution (`native_conversation_model`), never exact: a keyword also fires for people who never saw the ad.

connected.description: True when this profile already tracks the Page.

id.description: `outcome_events.id`. Pass this back as `payment_id` in every write on this surface.

amount.description: The payment's own value, in `currency`. Null when no amount was recorded.

operation_type.description: MercadoPago's `raw_data.operation_type`, or null for every other source.

name.description: `first_name` + `last_name`, either alone, or null when neither is known. Always null in a write's response when the caller lacks `customers:read`.

email.description: Always null in a write's response when the caller lacks `customers:read`.

customer_assigned_manually.description: Whether a merchant assignment (`PUT .../payer`) exists for this payment.

is_installment.description: A later installment of an earlier sale (`PUT .../installment`). Excluded from purchase COUNTS; still counted as cash.

counts_as_revenue.description: A conversion exists for this payment AND it is not suppressed.

excluded_reason.description: Why the payment does not count, when it does not: the conversion's `suppressed_reason`. `non_marketing_saas` = a GoHighLevel white-label SaaS charge (wallet recharge, plan) that no ad sells (#2053). Null when it counts or has no conversion yet.

refunded_amount.description: Positive sum of every reversal (provider + manual) keyed on this sale. `0` when unrefunded, never null.

amount.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

manual_refund.description: The merchant's own out-of-provider refund, or null when none is recorded.

id.description: The identity link. Accept or reject it with `POST /api/v1/identity/links/{id}/decide`.

method.description: How the link was made: `payer_name_booking` (inferred — same full name as exactly one customer who booked a call or became a lead in the 45 days before the payment) or `payer_email` (deterministic — the payment's email belongs to one customer, its phone or Checkout details to another).

status.description: `pending` = applied and awaiting review; `accepted` = confirmed. Rejected links are not published here.

name.description: The linked person's name. Null when unknown, or in a write's response when the caller lacks `customers:read`.

origin_event_at.description: When the linked person booked the call or became a lead (the link's evidence), or null.

payer_link.description: #2058 — the identity link tying this payer to the person who carries the ad origin, or null. Its only effect is that the payment may inherit that person's ad («vía lead»).

paid_with_other_email.description: #2058 — the payer's customer was found through the phone or the Checkout details, not the email this payment used. The email itself is never published here.

kind.description: `ad` starts the chain; then how the person reached the business (`instagram_dm`, `site_visit`, `crm_record` = the contact record carried the ad's click, …); then what they did before paying (`booking`, `skool_signup`, `signup`, `dm_started`); `payment` ends it.

method.description: `exact` = an identifier or an observed event; `inferred` = a match that is not an identifier (same name + booking, same name + Skool timing) or, on `payment`, credit carried from the person's lead rather than a click on this sale. Null on `ad` only.

payer.description: On `payment`: how the payment found the person.

id.description: The identity link. Accept or reject it with `POST /api/v1/identity/links/{id}/decide`.

method.description: How the link was made: `payer_name_booking` (inferred — same full name as exactly one customer who booked a call or became a lead in the 45 days before the payment) or `payer_email` (deterministic — the payment's email belongs to one customer, its phone or Checkout details to another).

status.description: `pending` = applied and awaiting review; `accepted` = confirmed. Rejected links are not published here.

name.description: The linked person's name. Null when unknown, or in a write's response when the caller lacks `customers:read`.

origin_event_at.description: When the linked person booked the call or became a lead (the link's evidence), or null.

payer_link.description: #2058 — the identity link tying this payer to the person who carries the ad origin, or null. Its only effect is that the payment may inherit that person's ad («vía lead»).

active_total.description: Effectively-active Meta ads (ad, ad set and campaign all ACTIVE).

examined.description: How many of those were examined — the busiest 500.

not_website.description: Ads whose clicks never reach a website (WhatsApp, instant forms, …).

not_synced.description: Ads whose template the nightly sync has not read yet — no verdict.

paid_touches.description: Paid browser Touches (Paid Social / Paid Search clicks) in the window.

with_ad_id.description: Of those, the ones whose ad the pipeline resolved.

coverage_pct.description: `with_ad_id / paid_touches × 100`, one decimal. Null when there were no paid Touches.

platform_clicks.description: The platform's own click count for the window, from synced delivery. Meta reports ALL clicks (likes and profile taps included), so this is context, not a denominator. Null when the platform has no delivery rows.

top_reason.description: The reason with the most misses; null when nothing is missing.

AdIdMissingCounts.description: Paid Touches without an ad id, by reason (every key always present). `unrendered_macro`: a UTM still contains `{{` — the link was opened outside the platform's substitution. `ad_id_not_in_catalog`: utm_content is an ad id no synced ad has (an unconnected ad account, or a deleted ad). `ad_name_not_matched`: utm_content is an ad NAME that could not be matched (renamed or duplicated ads). `no_ad_parameter`: campaign/ad-set parameters but no utm_content. `click_id_only`: no UTM parameters at all — only the platform click id. `no_tracking_parameters`: nothing in the URL; classified paid from the referrer or a channel rule.

clicks.description: Meta-reported clicks in the window — how much traffic the fix affects.

status.description: `ad_id_in_unread_param`: {{ad.id}} rides a parameter Atribu does not read. `ad_name_only`: the ad is named by {{ad.name}} only. `no_ad_macro`: URL parameters exist but none names the ad. `no_url_parameters`: the ad has none.

url_tags.description: The ad's current Meta URL parameters, verbatim.

suggested_url_tags.description: The ad's own parameters with Atribu's canonical ones applied — what to paste into the ad's URL parameters.

date_from.description: Applied start: the last 90 days of the requested range.

narrowed.description: True when the applied window is shorter than the requested one.

total.description: Browser Touches in the applied window.

classified.description: Of those, with a classified user agent — the denominator of every share.

itp_capped_pct.description: Share of classified Touches Safari's 7-day storage cap applies to (`webkit_browser` + `in_app_webkit`).

in_app_pct.description: Share inside an app's embedded browser, any OS.

allOf.description: Identified customers whose visits were all on standalone WebKit (`webkit`) or never on WebKit (`other`), and how many were seen under more than one visitor id.

mode.description: `same_origin_proxy`: a verified collector on the site's own domain — the only mode Safari does not cap. `cname_not_itp_proof`: a verified custom tracking domain (CNAME), which Safari still caps. `default`: Atribu's own collect endpoint.

configured.description: A same-origin collector address is saved (it may not have passed its check).

proxied_events.description: Events that arrived through this profile's authenticated collector.

with_server_cookie.description: Of those, from browsers that sent the server-set visitor cookie back.

proxy_traffic.description: The last 7 days of the collector's traffic; null when no collector secret exists.

recommendation.description: `install_same_origin_collector` / `replace_cname_with_same_origin`: enough traffic is capped to be worth the install. `finish_collector_check`: a collector is saved but has not passed its check. `route_tracker_through_collector`: verified, but no events reached it in 7 days. `none`: nothing to do.

ItpTouchesByClass.description: Every class, zero-filled. `webkit_browser`: Safari on any Apple device and every other iPhone/iPad browser. `in_app_webkit`: an app's embedded browser (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, …) on iPhone/iPad. `in_app_other`: an app's embedded browser elsewhere (Android). `other`: every other browser. `unknown`: no user agent.

allOf.description: Every non-WebKit browser.

sufficient.description: Both groups are large enough for the comparison to mean anything.

ItpComparison.description: Visitors (by the browser of their first visit) whose first visit is at least 14 days before the window ends, and how many came back more than 7 days later under the same visitor id. Safari forgets ids after 7 days, so a lower rate on WebKit is the cap made visible.

pct.description: `count / base × 100`, one decimal; null when `base` is 0.

ItpRate.description: Standalone WebKit: Safari on any Apple device and every iPhone/iPad browser.

currency.description: The profile's reporting currency.

atribu_windows.description: Atribu's own attribution windows for the profile.

rows_truncated.description: True when `rows` holds only the first 2,000 by spend.

reported_basis.description: What `platform_conversions` counts. `meta_standard_events`: Meta's standard-event rollups (purchase, lead, registration, schedule, contact, …) + messaging conversations started, under each ad set's attribution setting (default 7-day click + 1-day view — view-through and modeled conversions included). `google_conversions`: `metrics.conversions` (actions included in conversions, dated to the ad interaction). `tiktok_conversions`: TikTok's `conversion` metric. Null when no sync reports conversions for the platform.

in_catalog.description: Atribu holds this platform's campaigns — an ad account is or was connected.

has_delivery.description: Delivery (spend) was synced for this platform in the window.

delivery_through.description: Last day with synced delivery in the window.

value_unconverted_rows.description: Delivery rows whose conversion value could not be converted to the reporting currency (left out).

unassigned_conversions.description: Atribu conversions on this platform's paid clicks that name no entity at `level` (no ad id — see `GET /api/v1/quality/ad-ids`). NOT in the platform totals (which equal the sum of what its rows can hold), in no row.

spend.description: Spend on the reporting currency. Null when the platform delivered nothing in the window.

platform_conversions.description: The PLATFORM's own conversion count — its attribution, its windows, its dating. Null when the platform reports none (or delivered nothing). Can be fractional for Google (data-driven credit).

platform_conversion_value.description: The PLATFORM's own conversion value, converted to the reporting currency with the same FX as spend. Null when the platform reports no value (TikTok) or delivered nothing.

platform_purchases.description: Meta only: the purchase subset of `platform_conversions`.

platform_view_through_conversions.description: Google only: view-through conversions, which `platform_conversions` does NOT include.

atribu_conversions.description: Conversions Atribu credited here under `model` through a TRACED touch (every conversion type; reversals, installments and late-sibling suppressions excluded; credit inferred through the customer's lead is NOT here — see `atribu_inferred_conversions`). The same count `GET /api/v1/overview` publishes as `attributed_outcomes`. Under a multi-touch model one conversion can count on several rows.

atribu_cash_revenue.description: Cash Atribu credited here under `model` through a traced touch, refunds' negative credit included (inferred via-lead credit excluded — see `atribu_inferred_cash_revenue`). Only cash counts for ROAS.

atribu_inferred_conversions.description: Conversions credited here only by INFERENCE: a payment with no tracked touch of its own, credited to the ad that brought the same customer's lead. Shown beside `atribu_conversions`, never inside it.

atribu_inferred_cash_revenue.description: The cash of `atribu_inferred_conversions`. Never part of `atribu_cash_revenue` or `atribu_roas`.

conversion_gap.description: `atribu_conversions − platform_conversions`. Negative: the platform claims more than Atribu can trace.

conversion_gap_pct.description: `conversion_gap / platform_conversions × 100`, one decimal. Null when the platform reported 0 or nothing.

value_gap.description: `atribu_cash_revenue − platform_conversion_value`, exact. Null when the platform reports no value.

platform_roas.description: `platform_conversion_value / spend` — the ROAS the platform shows. Null without spend or value.

atribu_roas.description: `atribu_cash_revenue / spend` — cash ROAS by Atribu's attribution. Null without spend.

entity_id.description: The platform's own id for the campaign / ad set / ad.

has_delivery.description: The platform delivered this entity in the window. False: only Atribu credited it (e.g. a paused ad's late conversions).

spend.description: Spend on the reporting currency. Null when the platform delivered nothing in the window.

platform_conversions.description: The PLATFORM's own conversion count — its attribution, its windows, its dating. Null when the platform reports none (or delivered nothing). Can be fractional for Google (data-driven credit).

id.description: Stable per (profile, provider outcome): the same outcome always carries the same id, on the webhook, on every retry and on this replay. An attribution recompute or a re-sync never produces a second one. De-dupe on it.

provider.description: Always `atribu` (the platform provider every lifecycle event carries). The source is `data.provider`.

OutcomeRecordedEvent.description: A provider outcome recorded on an app-provisioned profile. For a healthcare-family profile only the app that provisioned it receives it. The `outcome.recorded` webhook body is this object plus `app_id` and `connection_id` (always `null`).

provider.description: The connection the outcome came from.

outcome_type.description: The outcome key: for GoHighLevel the stage mapping in force (`lead_created`, `appointment_booked`, `showed`, `qualified`, `closed_won`, `closed_lost`, …); for MercadoPago `payment_received`, `payment_refunded`, `payment_disputed`, ….

occurred_at.description: When the outcome happened at the provider (ISO 8601).

recorded_at.description: When Atribu recorded it. A first sync or backfill records old outcomes late, so `recorded_at` can be far after `occurred_at` — filter on `occurred_at` to skip history.

external_id.description: The provider's own id for this outcome (a GoHighLevel opportunity stage or contact, a MercadoPago payment).

outcome_event_id.description: Atribu's id for this outcome — the `outcome_event_id` `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/conversions` returns for the conversion it produced. Always joins.

conversion_id.description: The conversion this outcome produced — the `conversion_id` `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/conversions` returns, so the event joins to the campaign credited for it. Read at delivery / read time: `null` when the outcome produced no conversion, or none yet (conversions are extracted asynchronously, usually within seconds, so an early push can carry `null` where the replay later carries the id). Join on `outcome_event_id` when it is `null`.

customer_key.description: The provider's customer id (GoHighLevel contact id, MercadoPago payer). Only the provider's own opaque id shape rides freely (MercadoPago: digits; GoHighLevel: a letters-and-digits contact id); anything else (an email, any phone notation) is treated as contact data and served only with `customers:read` AND a live person (`contact` non-null), otherwise `null`.

amount.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

value.description: The outcome's value, when the provider states one (a payment, a won opportunity).

contact_withheld.description: `true` when the reader does not hold `customers:read` (webhook: the subscribing app's grant; replay: the calling key), so `contact` is `null` because of scope, not because no person is known. For a healthcare-family profile the replay decides it by the provisioning app's grant (the webhook's rule), since that app's key never carries `customers:read` there.

OutcomeRecordedContact.description: The person behind the outcome, read at delivery / read time (a redacted or erased person is `null`). Only with `customers:read`.

timezone.description: The profile's time zone. Every day and month boundary is in it.

buckets.description: Month and day buckets are dense (every bucket in the window, zeros included) and in calendar order. Ad buckets list every ad with an ad-touch person or Meta delivery in the window, by `ad_people` descending, up to `limit`.

buckets_truncated.description: True when `buckets` holds only the first `limit` ads.

origin_labels.description: Human labels (English and Spanish) for each `by_origin` key.

ad_people.description: Distinct people with at least one ad Touch in the bucket. Counts only: no person is ever returned.

ad_touches.description: Ad Touches in the bucket. With `first_only=true`, equal to `ad_people`.

meta_messaging_conversations_started.description: Meta's OWN reported count of messaging conversations started (`onsite_conversion.messaging_conversation_started_7d`) for the same bucket, summed from ad-level delivery by the ad account's own day. Shown so the gap between what Meta reports and the people Atribu can see is visible. Not narrowed by `channel` (Meta does not split it). Null, never 0, when there is no Meta delivery to report: none in the window, or for `group_by=ad`, none for that ad.

AdPeopleMeasures.description: The whole window, each person counted once. NOT the sum of the buckets: a person reached in two months is one person here and one in each month.

allOf.description: A WhatsApp or Instagram conversation Atribu received with Meta's ad referral attached.
A tracked website visit whose link named the ad.
Any other ad-tagged Touch: a CRM conversion's own ad parameters, a store journey, or a Touch inherited by a recurring payment.

AdPeopleByOrigin.description: The same people and Touches, split by where each Touch came from. A person reached through two origins counts in both, so the origins' `people` can add up to more than `ad_people`; their `touches` add up to `ad_touches` exactly.

people.description: Distinct people with at least one Touch of this origin in the bucket.

touches.description: Touches of this origin in the bucket.

AdPeopleOriginCount.description: Imported from a partner (historical): click-to-message ad referrals a partner handed over through `POST /api/v1/partner/ad-referrals` for conversations Atribu did not see live.

key.description: `YYYY-MM` for month, `YYYY-MM-DD` for day, the ad id for ad.

start.description: First day the bucket covers, clamped to the window.

end.description: Last day the bucket covers, clamped to the window.

ad_name.description: `group_by=ad` only: the ad's name from the ad catalog, else from delivery; null otherwise.

ad_people.description: Distinct people with at least one ad Touch in the bucket. Counts only: no person is ever returned.

ad_touches.description: Ad Touches in the bucket. With `first_only=true`, equal to `ad_people`.

meta_messaging_conversations_started.description: Meta's OWN reported count of messaging conversations started (`onsite_conversion.messaging_conversation_started_7d`) for the same bucket, summed from ad-level delivery by the ad account's own day. Shown so the gap between what Meta reports and the people Atribu can see is visible. Not narrowed by `channel` (Meta does not split it). Null, never 0, when there is no Meta delivery to report: none in the window, or for `group_by=ad`, none for that ad.

amount.description: Meta's `amount_spent` summed over the range, in `currency`.

currency.description: The WhatsApp Business Account's billing currency (ISO 4217); null when Meta did not report it.

clicks.description: Clicks per button over the range, most-clicked first.

daily.description: One entry per UTC day Meta reported, oldest first.

fetched_at.description: When Atribu read Meta (cached up to 15 minutes).

has_next.description: True when another page exists: request it with `cursor`.

cursor.description: Opaque. Pass it back unchanged as `?cursor=`. Absent on the last page.

recomputed_at.description: When the profile's attribution was last recomputed; null when never or on an empty page.

outcome_event_id.description: The outcome event this conversion was extracted from — the id Atribu returns at ingest (e.g. POST /api/v1/events). Null when the conversion has no outcome event behind it. `outcome_event_id ?? conversion_id` is a stable per-conversion key.

campaign_external_id.description: The winning campaign's platform id (the `campaign_external_id` of GET /api/v1/campaigns).

campaign_name.description: The campaign's current name, else the name on the touch, else its id.

credited_weight.description: The winning campaign's share of the conversion, 0–1: the sum of its touchpoints' credit, exactly the `credited_weight` GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/conversions returns for it.

credited_value.description: The winning campaign's credited share of the value, reporting currency.

touch_count.description: Touches in the conversion's whole path (`path_length`); `campaign_touch_count` when the path length is unknown.

campaign_touch_count.description: Credited touches on the winning campaign (the drill's `touch_count`).

first_touch_time.description: Earliest credited touch on the winning campaign.

last_touch_time.description: Latest credited touch on the winning campaign.

is_inherited.description: True when the winning campaign's credit came via a bridged lead→cash touch, not a directly-tracked click — never counted in ROAS.

value_amount.description: The conversion's full value (all of it, not the campaign's share), reporting currency.

currency.description: The reporting currency (ISO 4217).

customer_key.description: CRM contact id (not name/email) — the same field the per-campaign drill returns.

is_first_payment.description: Whether this payment is the customer's first. Null unless `revenue_type` is `cash`.

spend.description: Ad spend in the window. `null`, never `"0"`, exactly when `spend_available` is `false` — a measured zero still arrives as `"0"`. Read `spend_available` for WHY it is null.

spend_available.description: `false` when spend could not be scoped to the requested `filter[…]` set — either because a geo/device/browser/os dimension is not resolvable from an ad touch, or because the matching touches carry no ad ids at all. `spend`, `roas` and `clicks` are then `null`; this flag is the reason behind those nulls, not a substitute for reading them.

clicks.description: Ad clicks — the head of the conversion path. `null`, never `0`, exactly when `spend_available` is `false`.

revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

organic_direct_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

roas.description: Attributed revenue / spend. `null`, never `0`, exactly when `spend_available` is `false`. CAC, MER and NMER are not published — derive them from `spend` and the denominators here, and they inherit the null.

attributed_cash_outcomes.description: Attributed CASH outcomes only. NOT the CAC denominator — CAC is total spend / `first_payment_customers` (new customers, attributed or not). Divide spend by THIS and you get cost per ad-attributed cash payment, which on a low-coverage profile differs from CAC by two orders of magnitude.

cash_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

first_payment_revenue.description: Cash revenue from first payments only (the acquisition view).

first_payment_customers.description: Distinct customers whose first payment landed in this window. A count(DISTINCT), so NOT summable across `grain=day` buckets. A customer paying for several subjects (`subject_ref` on POST /api/v1/events) counts once per subject.

recurring_customers.description: Distinct repeat payers. count(DISTINCT); see `first_payment_customers`. A customer paying for several subjects (`subject_ref` on POST /api/v1/events) counts once per subject.

refund_amount.description: Refunded AMOUNT. Money nets, counts do not — these are two numbers.

dispute_reversed_amount.description: Amount of disputes later reversed in the merchant's favour. The engine exposes the amount but no matching count, so none is published.

outcome_counts.description: Conversions per conversion type, e.g. `{ "lead_created": 25 }`. Free-form: the set of types is per-profile configuration, not an enum.

days.description: One zero-filled row per calendar day in the requested window.

previous_days.description: The same series for the preceding window of equal length.

LtvDashboard.description: Null when the profile has no qualifying cohort data for the window.

total_cash.description: Cash revenue from payments in the window (#472 — LTV is cash-only, per data-model.md).

median_days_to_second.description: Median days between a customer's first and second payment. Null when no cohort has a repeat payer yet.

ltv.description: Cumulative cash LTV per customer at month m.

excluded.description: Cash in the window left OUT of `total` because no ad can sell it (`conversions.suppressed_reason`), keyed by that reason — `non_marketing_saas` is GoHighLevel white-label SaaS (#2053). `by_reason` is `{}` when nothing was excluded; null when the classification is unavailable.

event_id.description: The idempotency key this event is filed under.

outcome_event_id.description: The stored outcome event. The same id on every retry of the same key.

action.description: What the write did: `inserted` on the first delivery, `updated` on a retry, `enriched`/`skipped_lead_exists` on the one-lead-per-customer path.

customer_profile_id.description: The identity the sale was filed under, when one resolved. NULL is normal for an anon-only sale — it stays joinable by `anonymous_id`.

matched.description: Whether a conversion goal on this profile lists `event_name` in its `source_event_names`. FALSE means the event was stored but will never become a conversion and will never be attributed — fix the event name, or create the goal via `POST /api/v1/goals`.

event_name.description: The outcome type. Use `payment_received` for a closed sale where money changed hands (revenue_type `cash`, the only kind that counts toward ROAS) and `closed_won` for a won-but-unpaid deal (revenue_type `pipeline`). Any other name is accepted, but unless a conversion goal lists it in `source_event_names` the event becomes no conversion at all — check `conversion.matched` in the response.

anonymous_id.description: The Atribu tracker's visitor id (`atribu_visitor_id` cookie / `atribu_anon_id`), when your checkout captured it. The most direct sale↔click link there is: it needs no email match.

session_id.description: The tracker's session id, when captured. Links the sale to one specific visit.

timestamp.description: When the sale closed (ISO-8601). Defaults to now. Send the ERP's own timestamp: it must be stable across retries, and it is what the attribution window is measured against.

properties.description:
Free-form payload, stored verbatim on the outcome event. `value` (or `amount`) and `currency` are read out of it: `value` is the sale amount as a number or numeric string, `currency` an ISO-4217 code (defaults to USD). A `value` that is present but unparseable is a 400, never a silent zero.

`subject_ref` (optional) is the opaque id of WHO a payment is for, when one customer pays for several — e.g. a parent paying for each child's treatment at a clinic. Send a canonical UUID (8-4-4-4-12 hex — your internal patient uuid) or a short token of up to 32 letters, digits, `_` and `-`. A value is rejected with 400 if it contains an `@`, 7 or more digits in a row once separators (including a single letter between digits) are removed (a RUT/RUN, a phone, a compact date), a date, a name, or a 32/40/64-hex digest. Those checks catch mistakes; they cannot detect every name or a hashed or encoded personal identifier, so `subject_ref` MUST be an opaque id — your obligation under the data-processing agreement. Each distinct `subject_ref` under one customer gets its own first payment — so a second patient's first treatment counts as a new customer, ships to ad platforms as a `Purchase` and is credited to its own ad — but only if every EARLIER payment of that customer carries a different `subject_ref`: an earlier untagged payment makes the new subject a returning one, so turning the field on never inflates new customers. To have past patients counted correctly, re-send their historical payments with the same idempotency key plus `subject_ref` BEFORE sending new ones. A retry that omits `subject_ref` removes it from the stored event and the payment is regrouped as untagged. A household whose earlier payments came from an integration (MercadoPago, Webpay, CSV import, Shopify — sources that cannot carry a subject) keeps the per-customer rule, and an untagged payment after a tagged one is never a first payment, even within the usual 7-day grouping. Omit it entirely and the payment behaves exactly as before. It is used only inside Atribu: it is never sent to Meta, Google or TikTok, never returned by any API, and it is erased with the customer.

campaign.description: For Meta, the campaign's numeric platform id.

content.description: For Meta, the AD's numeric platform id.

term.description: For Meta, the AD SET's numeric platform id.

id.description: `utm_id`. For Meta, the campaign's numeric platform id (`utm_id={{campaign.id}}`). Stored with the other UTMs; when it matches a synced campaign it decides the sale's campaign even if `campaign` is a name shared by several campaigns.

utm.description: The marketing parameters the buyer arrived with, if your ERP recorded them. Used to build a synthetic touch for a sale that never had a web session.

click_ids.description: Ad-platform click ids captured at the landing page. `fbclid`, `gclid`, `msclkid` and `ttclid` are joined against the click index to recover the originating session for up to 90 days; any other kind is stored for later.

action_source.description: Where the outcome really happened, in Meta's `action_source` vocabulary. Sent to Meta verbatim on every Conversions API export of this event, whatever the privacy mode. Any value other than `website` ships with NO `event_source_url` (not even the origin), even when the buyer has fbc/fbp browser signals — a sale recorded in a CRM or at a counter is not a website event, and for a health business the domain in the URL is what Meta categorizes a data source by. Pick: `business_messaging` for an outcome born in a WhatsApp/Messenger/Instagram conversation (with `click_ids.ctwa_clid` when the chat came from a click-to-WhatsApp ad, it is exported to the dataset linked to your WhatsApp Business Account; without a WABA-linked dataset or a click id it is sent as `chat`, because Meta rejects a `business_messaging` event that carries no messaging click id); `physical_store` for a payment taken in person; `system_generated` for a fact your system derived (an appointment confirmed, a status change); `website` only for an event that happened on your site. Omit it to keep the previous inference: `business_messaging` on a WhatsApp dataset with a click id, else `website` when browser signals exist, else `system_generated`.

marketing.description: `false` marks this event LEDGER ONLY (#1651): it still attributes and counts toward revenue and ROAS exactly like any other event, but it is never exported to Meta CAPI, Google Ads or TikTok — the tracking-exports candidate builder drops it before any outbound call, with the distinct reason `ledger_only_no_export`. Omitted or `true` exports normally, same as before this field existed. Send `false` whenever the buyer opted out of marketing — e.g. a health-restricted profile in `platform_safe` mode where the clinic still needs cash ROAS per campaign but the patient must produce no CAPI event.

consent.description: Per-event export consent. An object, not a single top-level flag, so a later consent dimension (e.g. an analytics-only opt-out) can be added without a breaking change to this endpoint.

idempotency_key.description: The sale's own deal/order id. Retries with the same key land on the same outcome event — `external_id` is `api:<key>`. REQUIRED whenever `properties.value` is set: without it the key defaults to a fresh UUID, so a retried sale would be counted twice, and double-counted cash cannot be undone from the data. Also accepted as the `Idempotency-Key` header.

IngestEventBody.description: A server-side outcome event. The worked example is the sale-closed case: a dealer's ERP reporting a paid sale with the identity signals needed to join it back to the ad click.

email.description: Buyer email. Normalised and resolved through the identity graph, which is how an off-site sale reaches the ad click captured on the website.

phone.description: Buyer phone. Normalised to E.164 when parseable.

external_id.description: YOUR customer id (the ERP/CRM primary key), stored as an `external_customer_id` identifier so repeat sales from the same buyer converge on one customer profile. On its own it is used for a READ-ONLY lookup: an identifier with no email or phone never creates a profile, because a profile minted from a foreign key alone can never be merged with the real one later.

national_id.description: A government identity document number (e.g. a Chilean RUT) — the phone↔RUT↔email bridge a clinic's own practice-management software already holds. Normalised and stored as a `national_id` identifier, the same type MercadoPago's own `payer.identification` writes, so it is used as a match key alongside email and phone: unlike `external_id`, a `national_id` with no email or phone still creates a profile. An SII **generic receptor** RUT — `66.666.666-6` (boleta de ventas y servicios), `55.555.555-5` (export / Factura Especial Turista) or `44.444.446-0` (boleta de honorarios to a foreigner) — is IGNORED: those are the values a document carries when the issuer did not record who the customer is, they all pass the mod-11 check, and storing one would merge every anonymous customer of a profile onto a single non-person.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 hint for parsing `national_id`. Defaults to `CL` — the only country national_id parsing understands today.

IngestEventUserTraits.description: Identity signals. At least one of these — or `anonymous_id`, or a click id — is what makes the sale attributable; a sale with none of them is recorded but can never be joined to an ad.

results.description: One entry per request row, in the SAME order — degrade visibly, never drop.

index.description: The row's position in the request's `rows` array.

reason.description: Present only on a `rejected` row — why it was rejected.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 hint for the WHOLE batch's `national_id` (and phone) parsing — one CSV is one clinic, one country. Defaults to `CL`.

CustomerImportBody.description: A batch of customer identities from the clinic's own records — a PMS export or a spreadsheet, not an event.

national_id.description: A government identity document number (e.g. a Chilean RUT). Normalised exactly like `user_traits.national_id` on POST /api/v1/events, SII generic receptor RUTs included — a row whose only identity is one of those is REJECTED with a reason naming it, never silently imported.

external_id.description: YOUR customer id (PMS/CRM primary key). Never enough on its own — a row with no phone, email or national_id is REJECTED, because a profile minted from a foreign key alone can never be merged with the real one later.

attribution_carrier.description: Which field the visitor identity was recovered from. NULL means the passthrough carried nothing and the sale falls back to an email/phone match — check that your `Transaction.create()` really sent `getAttributionRef()` as `session_id`.

anonymous_id.description: The visitor the sale was tied to, decoded from the carrier.

forwarded.description: true when the read receipt (plus the typing indicator, unless `indicator: "read"`) reached Meta. false when Meta refused the `message_id` (stale / already-read / re-registered number) — a knowing no-op, still a 200.

indicator.description: The mode that was applied, echoed back. Absent means the deployment predates this field and therefore behaved as `typing` — the only way to detect that a requested `read` silently showed a bubble.

reason.description: Present only when `forwarded` is false. `stale_message_id` — Meta refused the wamid. `message_id_conversation_mismatch` — the wamid belongs to a different conversation than `to`, so it was never forwarded.

expires_at.description: ISO timestamp at which `url` stops working.

sha256.description: Meta's SHA-256 (hex) of the media bytes — verify what `url` serves. Null when Meta sent none.

file_size.description: Size in bytes (Meta's `file_size`, else the bytes Atribu stored).

status.description: DRAFT | PUBLISHED | DEPRECATED | BLOCKED | THROTTLED (Meta-owned enum).

categories.description: Typed loosely on reads — Meta may add categories.

validation_errors.description: Meta's flow.json validation findings, forwarded verbatim. Empty when valid.

preview.description: Web preview URL for the flow (renders in a browser).

can_send_message.description: AVAILABLE | LIMITED | BLOCKED — the overall verdict (Meta-owned enum).

errors.description: Present when the node is BLOCKED.

additional_info.description: Present when the node is LIMITED.

health_status.description: Meta's sendability verdict for the flow, forwarded verbatim: an overall `can_send_message` plus one entry per node a send involves (FLOW, WABA, BUSINESS, APP). The FLOW node is LIMITED while the flow is THROTTLED (10 sends/hour) and BLOCKED while it is BLOCKED, DEPRECATED, or unpublished with a failing publishing check. Changes are also pushed as the `whatsapp.flow.status` / `whatsapp.flow.alert` webhook events.

download_url.description: Time-limited URL to download the asset bytes.

endpoint_uri.description: The URL to set as the flow's `endpoint_uri` (create/update a flow with it). Meta calls it; Atribu verifies Meta's signature, decrypts, and forwards to `data_url`.

data_url.description: Partner HTTPS URL Atribu forwards each decrypted Flow request to.

enabled.description: When false, data requests answer 500 to Meta (pings and error notifications are still answered).

signing_secret.description: HMAC secret for the `X-Atribu-Signature` header on the data hop (64 hex chars). Present ONLY when it was just minted (first registration) or rotated — store it; it cannot be read again.

status.description: Meta's view of Atribu's business public key for the number. Only `VALID` can serve published flows.

last_error.description: Last key-sync or data-hop failure, if any. Never contains payloads.

canSend.description: Meta's overall `can_send_message`, or null when `health_status` could not be read. null means unknown, never healthy.

refreshedAt.description: When this snapshot was last read from Meta (ISO). null on a never-refreshed account.

stale.description: True when this snapshot was NOT confirmed against Meta just now — either it is older than the 6h TTL and a revalidation was throttled, or a revalidation ran and its live read failed, so these are last-good values. Treat it as "the last thing we knew", never as a verification. A successful live/forced refresh returns false.

reconnectRequired.description: True when the channel needs re-authorization (invalid/expired token).

reconnectUrl.description: Where to send the user to reconnect the WhatsApp channel, or null when not required.

code.description: Meta's own error code (number), a synthetic code (`token_invalid`), or null when Meta gave none.

message.description: Meta's error message (or Atribu's, for a synthetic code).

refreshError.description: Why the last live read did NOT verify this snapshot. null exactly when it did. On a failed `refresh=true` this is set (with `stale:true`, `canSend:null` and a `health_unverified` issue) instead of silently serving the cached row; a confirmed dead token carries `tokenValid:false`, `reconnectRequired:true` and `code:"token_invalid"` or Meta's code. `refreshedAt` only advances when Meta confirmed the snapshot (a live success or a confirmed dead token), so it is safe to apply a staleness rule to it.

entityType.description: Meta entity_type (PHONE_NUMBER, MESSAGE_TEMPLATE, WABA, BUSINESS, APP) or a synthetic bucket (APP) for token/webhook issues.

code.description: Meta error_code (number), a synthetic string code, or null for advisories.

remediation.description: Meta's `possible_solution`, or Atribu's remediation for synthetic issues.

WhatsAppCallingSettings.description: Meta's `calling` object, passed through verbatim in both directions. Atribu holds no opinion about its contents — the SIP peer, the SRTP key exchange and the codec list are the caller's recipe. Documented as free-form on purpose: a schema enumerating Meta's fields would reject a field Meta shipped this morning.

sip_user_password.description: Meta-generated digest password for this SIP peer.

media_url.description: Short-lived CDN URL, or null when Meta omits it. A CAROUSEL_ALBUM parent may carry its own cover URL or not — read `children` for the per-item URLs rather than relying on the parent.

children.description: Ordered carousel items; null for non-carousel media.

id.description: Conversation id — pass to the messages endpoint.

updated_time.description: When the last message was added. This is a LAST-ACTIVITY stamp: Meta exposes no conversation-creation time, so it cannot tell you how far back a thread goes.

id.description: IGSID of the participant (or the account's own id).

message.description: Text body, or null when Meta withheld it — the documented outcome for any message past the 20 most recent in the thread. The id and created_time still identify the message.

is_unsupported.description: Meta returns this only when true.

InstagramMessageAttachment.description: Meta returns only a URL for shared media — a shared post or reel does not come back as a re-hostable asset.

update_time.description: Epoch ms of the conversation's last message.

referral.description: Every Click-to-Message ad / TikTok.me link the conversation was entered from, as TikTok returned them; null when none.

ad_id.description: Manual ad id, an ad in a Smart+ campaign, or a creative in an Upgraded Smart+ ad.

profile_image.description: Temporary URL; re-read after it expires.

reason.description: Why it is closed; null when open.

merchant_label.description: Which Merchant this app was made available to — the Shopify API Terms §2.3.20 audit trail.

plus_org_id.description: Non-null asserts every bound store belongs to ONE Shopify Plus organization, which is the only case §2.3.20 permits a Custom Application to serve more than one store.

scopes.description: The exact OAuth scopes this app's authorize URL requests. `read_all_orders` is approval-gated PER APP by Shopify, so a freshly registered custom-distribution app defaults to `SHOPIFY_OAUTH_SCOPES` minus the gated scopes — asking for one the app has not been approved for makes Shopify 400 the authorize URL before the merchant sees a consent screen. Widen it with PATCH once Shopify approves the access request.

credited_revenue.description: Revenue credited to this touch under the profile's default model.

credit_weight.description: Fraction of the conversion's credit this touch received (0–1).

recommended.description: There is an open scale/optimize/kill recommendation for this ad.

data_quality_tier.description: Which signal drives the numbers: cash / outcomes / engagement / meta_only / none.

spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

high_intent_band.description: Wilson-confidence band on `high_intent_rate` — a small-sample ad reads `low` even with a flattering rate.

cost_per_high_intent.description: The hero metric: spend ÷ qualified conversations.

attributed_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

expected_impact_dollars.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

ad_id.description: Meta's own ad id — the same `platform_id` a `GET /api/v1/campaigns?level=ad` row and `ad_external_id` on top-performers carry, and the `{id}` `POST /api/v1/ads/{id}/pause` takes. Never an internal uuid.

adset_id.description: Meta's own ad-set id — the `{id}` `POST /api/v1/adsets/{id}/budget` takes. Never an internal uuid.

ad_name.description: Display name of the target ad. NULL when the recommendation targets no ad. Render this, never `target.ad_id` — an ad id is not something a person can recognise.

expected_impact_dollars.description: Arithmetic on the ad's OWN observed unit economics over the next 7 days, under the stated assumption that the extra budget performs like the window did. Phrase it with "if" — it is not a forecast.

realized_impact_dollars.description: What the apply actually produced. NULL until measured — which is not zero, and a surface that shows only `expected_impact_dollars` is reporting a hope as a result.

calibration_error.description: `realized - expected`, in the same units. NULL until measured.

data_quality_tier.description: What evidence the recommendation rests on — `cash` / `outcomes` / `engagement` / `meta_only` / `none`. The same ladder `truth_grade` walks for a leaderboard row.

replayed.description: True when the executor's deterministic key found this leg already written at Meta.

session_join_method.description: The Atribu tier that produced the linkage, even when `join_method` is `ctwa_referral`.

ambiguous.description: True when more than one distinct visitor matched — a deliberate non-join.

conversation_started.description: Whether this call wrote (or changed) the outcome event.

attribution_deferred.description:
#1550 — the join was ACCEPTED and recorded in Atribu's messaging core, but the outcome event that carries it into attribution could not be written yet because Atribu's analytics store did not answer. The work is parked durably and replayed automatically, on the same key the outcome row uses, so nothing is duplicated and nothing is lost.

`conversation_started` is then `false` and `outcome_event_id` is `null` whatever the replay eventually produces: this response says what Atribu knew at the time. **Do not retry on it** — a retry re-parks the same row and buys nothing. Every other field is fully resolved: the join tiers read the messaging core, which is the project that answered this request.

`false` on every response from a healthy Atribu.

merchant_phone.description: The number the message was sent TO. Digits or E.164.

sender_phone.description: The number it came FROM. Optional — a join can succeed on text alone.

message_text.description: The message body, verbatim. Normalisation happens server-side.

occurred_at.description: The MESSAGE's own timestamp, ISO-8601 — never receipt time. A backlog drain stamped with flush time would miss every correlation window.

ctwa_clid.description: Meta's click-to-WhatsApp click id, when the conversation came from a CTWA ad.

token.description: An explicit `[#ABC123]`, when the caller stripped it out of the body itself.

attributed_credited_conversions.description: Directly-tracked credited conversions on ATTRIBUTED campaigns only (the unattributed bucket excluded). Every other field here is a plain sum over `campaigns`; this one is the number Atribu's own Attribution view puts in its KPI strip.

Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

direct_cash_value.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

inherited_cash_value.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

campaign_external_id.description: Platform-side campaign id, or `__unattributed__` for the bucket holding conversions with no campaign-bearing touch.

credited_conversions.description: Sum of credit_weight. A conversion's weights sum to 1 across its whole path under every model, so this is fractional under linear / time_decay and whole under last_touch.

total_value.description: Credit-weighted value across all revenue types (cash + pipeline).

cash_value.description: The cash subset of total_value (direct + inherited).

direct_cash_value.description: Directly-tracked cash. The ONLY cash that belongs in a ROAS numerator — inherited (bridged lead→cash) credit is reported separately and never summed in.

inherited_cash_value.description: Cash credited via a bridged lead→cash touch. Never in ROAS.

get.summary: Get an ad's AI creative analysis

The stored AI analysis of one ad's creative — its angle, offer, hook and claim style, plus (for video ads) a verbatim transcript and a beat-by-beat scene timeline. `{id}` is the ad's EXTERNAL (platform) id, the same value `GET /api/v1/top-performers` returns as `ad_external_id`.

**This is a read, never a run.** The analysis is produced by a scheduled daily background pass and this endpoint serves what that pass already stored; it issues no model call, counts against no allowance, and cannot be used to trigger one. Two consequences follow. Coverage is not guaranteed: an ad the pass has not reached — including every ad on a profile where the pass is switched off — answers 404 with `code: "not_found"`, distinct in message from an ad id that does not belong to this key's profile. And freshness is the pass's, not the request's: read `analyzed_at`.

`method` tells you which tier produced the row and therefore how much of `video` is populated. Embeddings and the derived per-role duration scalars are deliberately not published — they are ML ranker inputs, and `video.scenes` carries the same observations in the form they were made.
