post.summary: Record a customer's "how did you find us?" answer from your WhatsApp conversation
post.description:
For a partner that asks the question inside its OWN WhatsApp conversation and interprets the reply. The answer is stored in the declared-source store with `origin = whatsapp` and `collected_via = partner`, and shows up in `GET /api/v1/attribution/declared-source` beside click attribution. It is never a touch and never changes credit.

**Scoping.** No `profile_id`: the key is the tenant, exactly as on `POST /api/v1/partner/wa-joins`. `merchant_phone` / `waba_id` must name one of that profile's WhatsApp accounts (`404` otherwise), and that account must have the question switched on (`PATCH /api/v1/whatsapp/declared-source-prompt`, `403` otherwise).

**The customer** is exactly one of `external_ref` (your own customer id) or `wa_id` (resolved from the phone). A known `external_ref` resolves read-only. To backfill answers for people Atribu has never seen, send `email` and/or `phone` with the `external_ref`: Atribu resolves or creates the customer from that PII and binds the ref, exactly as `POST /api/v1/events` does for `user_traits.external_id`. A ref alone never creates a customer. Both forms work on healthcare-family profiles; a national id (RUT) is never accepted.

**Idempotent — retry it.** Keyed on `wamid`, and WhatsApp's unit is the customer: one answer per customer per profile, first wins.

Scope: `whatsapp` (a partner connection's token) or `events:write`.

400.description: Malformed body — including both or neither customer form, `asked_at` after `answered_at`, a malformed `email` / `phone`, or a national id (`invalid_parameter`: a `national_id` / `rut` key, or a RUT-shaped `external_ref` / `phone`)

403.description: `insufficient_scope`; `forbidden` — the question is off for this WhatsApp account

404.description: No WhatsApp account on the key's profile matches `merchant_phone` / `waba_id`

409.description: `entitlement_required` — an `events:write` key on a profile without the attribution entitlement

422.description: `unknown_answer_key`, or `unknown_customer_ref` — `external_ref` names no live customer on this profile and no `email` / `phone` came with it

503.description: Transient — retry with the same body

post.summary: Record a historical click-to-message ad referral
post.description:
For a business moving to Atribu from another WhatsApp bot: tell Atribu which Meta ad a PAST conversation came from, so the ad gets the credit it earned before Atribu was connected.

**What it records.** A touch at `occurred_at` naming the ad (campaign and ad set resolved from Atribu's Meta sync), judged by the profile's own attribution windows — a later conversion is credited to it only inside them (click window for last touch, first-touch window for first touch). That is how a later `closed_won` or `payment_received` is credited to the ad that started the conversation.

**No lead.** It never creates a `lead_created` and never changes an existing lead, so the customer's next lead is recorded — and exported — normally. Leads from before Atribu was connected are not reconstructed.

**Nothing from this call is sent to Meta.** A touch is never exported, and the click id stays with the touch: it is not stored on the customer, so it never rides a later conversion to Meta.

**Scoping and the customer** work exactly as on `POST /api/v1/partner/declared-source`: the key is the tenant, `merchant_phone` / `waba_id` must name one of that profile's WhatsApp accounts, and the customer is `external_ref` (with `email` / `phone` to create someone Atribu has never seen) or `wa_id`. A national id (RUT) is never accepted.

**Idempotent — retry it.** Keyed on `idempotency_key`.

**Preview first.** `POST /api/v1/partner/ad-referrals/preview` reports, with no writes, which existing conversions a batch would re-credit.

Scope: `whatsapp` (a partner connection's token) or `events:write`.

400.description: Malformed body — both or neither customer form, a non-numeric `ad_id`, `ctwa_clid` on a non-WhatsApp channel, an `occurred_at` in the future, or a national id (`invalid_parameter`)

404.description: No WhatsApp account on the key's profile matches `merchant_phone` / `waba_id`

409.description: `entitlement_required` — an `events:write` key on a profile without the attribution entitlement; `idempotency_key_conflict` — the key was already used for a different referral; `idempotency_key_in_flight` — a first request with the key is still running (retry shortly)

422.description: `unknown_ad` — `ad_id` is not one of the profile's Meta ads; `unknown_customer_ref` — `external_ref` names no live customer and no `email` / `phone` came with it

503.description: Transient — retry with the same body

post.summary: Preview what a batch of historical ad referrals would re-credit
post.description:
Read-only. Takes up to 500 referrals in the shape `POST /api/v1/partner/ad-referrals` takes and reports, without creating a customer or writing anything, how applying them would change credit: how many of the named customers' existing conversions would gain a touch inside the profile's attribution windows, and — per attribution model — how many would change the ad they credit. Run it before a backfill.

Scope: `whatsapp` (a partner connection's token) or `events:write`.

200.description: The impact of applying the batch

400.description: Malformed body — both or neither customer form, a non-numeric `ad_id`, `ctwa_clid` on a non-WhatsApp channel, an `occurred_at` in the future, or a national id (`invalid_parameter`)

404.description: No WhatsApp account on the key's profile matches `merchant_phone` / `waba_id`

409.description: `entitlement_required` — an `events:write` key on a profile without the attribution entitlement

422.description: `unknown_customer_ref` — an `external_ref` names no live customer and no `email` / `phone` came with it

503.description: Transient — retry with the same body

get.summary: Read the customer-list audience
get.description: The state of this profile's Meta customer list of the people who PAID in the last 365 days, and of its 1 % lookalike — and whether the profile can have one at all (`available`, `reason`). Use it as the capability check before offering the feature. Requires `exports:read`.

post.summary: Create the customer-list audience
post.description:
Creates, once per profile, a Meta Custom Audience named «Vitrina · Clientes que pagaron» (the name is fixed by Atribu and is never taken from the request) holding the people who paid this profile in the last 365 days (net of refunds and disputes; merged duplicates count as one person), and runs its first upload. What is sent is the column set the recorded consent version covers (`USER_PROVIDED_ONLY`, `CUSTOM`): under the current text (v2), hashed e-mail, phone, first name, last name and country from each member's own customer record (the guardian's when a guardian paid); a list created under v1 keeps sending hashed e-mail and phone only. Never a national id or an amount. People with a marketing opt-out, erased customers, merged duplicates and customers your app marked (`PUT /api/v1/profiles/{profileId}/audience-exclusions`) are left out. There is no fallback to leads or appointments. Atribu replaces the members nightly.

**Consent.** `consent` must name the current published consent text (`version` and the SHA-256 of one locale's text, `@atribu/api-contract` `CUSTOMER_LIST_AUDIENCE_CONSENT_*`), rendered verbatim and accepted by the business owner. A missing, older or foreign one is `409 consent_required`, before any Meta call. A new list needs the current version (v2). A list already live under v1 keeps uploading only what v1 covers, and re-POSTing its v1 acceptance stays idempotent; a `POST` with the v2 consent re-records it on the list (nothing is re-created).

**Lookalike.** With `lookalike: { ratio: 0.01, country }` the 1 % lookalike is created too, or recorded as `waiting_size` while the list has fewer than ~100 people.

**Idempotent** per profile: a second call returns the existing audience without creating or uploading again. An `Idempotency-Key` header is honoured on top. Requires `exports:write`.

202.description: The audience exists in Meta and its upload landed; Meta is still matching it.

409.description: `consent_required`: no consent, or not the current text (`error.consent` names the current version and hashes). `invalid_state` with `reason`: not available for this profile (the `reason` values of the read).

422.description: `validation_error`: a malformed body, or a lookalike that is not `{ ratio: 0.01, country }`.

502.description: `provider_error`: Meta refused the create or the upload. Retry; nothing is created twice.

delete.description: Stops it: the lookalike and then the list are DELETED in Meta, not merely orphaned, and the nightly refresh stops. Works even after the feature was switched off for the profile. Answers the final state; with nothing to delete, `200` with `audience: null`. Requires `exports:write`.

409.description: `invalid_state`: the Meta connection the audience was created on is not usable, so it cannot be deleted in Meta. Nothing was marked deleted.

502.description: `provider_error`: Meta refused a delete. Anything already deleted stays deleted; retry.

post.summary: Add the 1 % lookalike
post.description: Adds the one lookalike («Vitrina · Parecidos a clientes que pagaron (1 %)») to an existing customer list. Below ~100 people it is recorded as `waiting_size` and created by the nightly refresh. A second call is a no-op. Requires `exports:write`.

409.description: `invalid_state`: not available (`reason`), `no_customer_list`, or a lookalike for another country exists (`lookalike_exists`).

422.description: `validation_error`: not `{ ratio: 0.01, country }`.

put.summary: Keep customers out of every audience
put.description:
Marks (or unmarks) customers of a profile your app provisioned so they are never in a Meta audience Atribu builds, starting with the customer-list audience. The mark is generic: Atribu attaches no meaning to it and infers nothing. Who carries it is your decision, and a customer you do not mark is not excluded.

Each row names one customer the way the other partner routes do (`customer_key`, `email`, `phone`, or `identifier_type` + `identifier_value`) and states the end state in `excluded`. **Idempotent**: replaying a body changes nothing, and within one body the last row naming a customer wins. A row naming nobody answers `not_found`: no customer is ever created, so mark a customer again once it has reached Atribu. A mark set on a customer that is later merged keeps the merged customer out. Up to 1,000 rows per call; send a longer list as several calls.

App credential (HTTP Basic `client_id:client_secret`); only profiles your app provisioned. Any other profile, archived or unknown, answers `404`.

400.description: `validation_error`: no `customers`, more than 1,000, or a malformed row. `invalid_request`: not JSON.

404.description: `not_found`: not a profile your app provisioned

503.description: `database_unavailable`: Atribu's database could not be reached mid-request. Retry the same body after `Retry-After` seconds; the call is idempotent, so a partly applied batch converges.

Each carries its DPA state and how many of the profiles it provisioned the acceptance covers. Readable by any member of the workspace. An API key cannot call it: a key is minted for one profile and belongs to no workspace.

post.summary: Accept the DPA for every profile an OAuth app provisions
post.description:
Accepts Atribu's Data Processing Agreement ONCE for a partner app. A partner that provisions headless profiles for its own customers (`POST /api/v1/profiles`) is the DPA counterparty for those profiles — its customers never sign in to Atribu — so the acceptance is written through, in the same transaction, to every profile the app provisioned (`dpa_status = accepted` with this version, time and acceptor), and every profile it provisions later is accepted at birth. A profile whose own owner already accepted directly keeps that acceptance.

**Idempotent.** Accepting an app that is already accepted writes no new signature and keeps the original `dpa_accepted_at`; it still re-applies the acceptance to any provisioned profile that lacks it.

`document_version` names which shipped DPA text you displayed; it is checked against the same allowlist as the profile click-wrap. Omit it to accept the current full text.

**A signed-in owner or admin of this workspace, in a browser session.** An `atb_live_` API key never reaches this route, and an MCP `atb_user_` token is refused with `403 insufficient_scope`: a token is the credential its owner minted for an agent, and an agent cannot agree to a contract on the partner's behalf. The same rule as `POST /api/v1/legal/dpa/accept`.

post.summary: Withdraw an OAuth app's DPA acceptance

Withdraws the app-level acceptance. get.summary: Which single creative-dimension values win in this workspace
get.description:
The DIMENSION-grain companion to `/creative-patterns`. That route mines (hook × format × cta) COMBINATIONS and tells you who is not running them; this one takes one dimension at a time — hook type, narrative arc, CTA and so on — and answers how often an ad carrying a given value ends up a winner.

**The lift is an ASSOCIATION.** `lift_vs_workspace` is the row's win rate over the workspace's own baseline, and `confidence_interval_low`/`_high` is the interval that estimate sits in. Rendering the lift without the interval reports a point estimate as a fact — and neither is a causal claim. The only causal evidence on this surface is an experiment (`/experiments`).

`min_cluster_size` (3–50, default 3) is an honesty floor, not a page size: below it a win rate is dominated by its own sample noise. Lowering it does not reveal more patterns, it reveals more coin flips.

**Session bearers only.** An API key is minted for exactly one profile — the credential IS the scope — so it has no workspace to read across and this route answers `403 insufficient_scope` for one. Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses).

A workspace owner, admin or analyst sees every profile in the workspace; anyone else sees only the profiles they hold a membership on. That narrowing happens in the database, not in the response shape, so a guest gets a 200 over a smaller set — never someone else's rows.

get.description:

None of the six is a lifetime total: `top_performer_count` is ads performing like top performers *in this window* and `at_risk_count` is ads whose predicted hazard crossed a tier *in this window*, so rendering them beside a lifetime figure compares two different questions.

`lift_backed_count` is the one to read first — how many ads have an EXPERIMENT behind them rather than a score. It is normally small, and that is the true state.

get.summary: The signed-in user's own account
get.description:
Who the caller is, how they can sign in, where they are signed in, and what would block them from deleting the account — in one round trip, because a settings surface wants all four at once.

`user` is the editable identity (`PATCH /api/v1/me` changes `full_name` and `locale`). `identities` is the auth-provider list — provider keys and the address each provider knows, never a token. `sessions` is one row per signed-in device, freshest first, with `is_current` resolved from the bearer token this request carried. `sole_owner_workspaces` names the workspaces whose ownership would be orphaned by a deletion.

**App credentials get a different, smaller answer (#1048).** An OAuth app's own HTTP Basic `client_id:client_secret` — the credential `POST /api/v1/profiles` and `POST /api/v1/workspaces` accept — receives `{ data: { app, return_url_supported } }` with no `meta`, since the caller is a credential, not a person. `return_url_supported` is the one fact a consumer needs before passing a `return_url` to any connect start.

Everything here is the CALLER'S OWN data, resolved from the verified token and from nothing the request asserted. There is no parameter naming a user, so reading someone else's account is not expressible — which is also why no PII scope gates it.

**Session bearers only.** An API key is minted for exactly one profile — it is not a person, has no sessions and no linked identities — so this route answers `403 insufficient_scope` for one. Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses).

200.description: The caller's account (session bearer), or `{ data: { app, return_url_supported } }` for an app credential

403.description: The credential is an API key (single-profile by design)

patch.summary: Update the signed-in user's display name or locale
patch.description:
A partial update: omit a field to leave it alone. Both fields live in Atribu's own `user_profiles`, so neither triggers a Supabase Auth flow and neither sends mail.

**Email and password are NOT here** — see `POST /api/v1/me/password` and the `/api/v1/me/email` pair below. Each is a real GoTrue flow (a breach check and a rate-limited re-authentication for the password; a dual-confirmation mail for the email) with its own request shape, so neither fits a partial PATCH of two plain columns.

Returns the updated `user` object — the same shape `GET /api/v1/me` nests under `user`.

**Session bearers only.** An API key is minted for exactly one profile — it is not a person, has no sessions and no linked identities — so this route answers `403 insufficient_scope` for one. Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses).

403.description: The credential is an API key (single-profile by design)

delete.description:
Three steps, server-side: re-check `sole_owner_workspaces` FRESH (a client's own copy may be stale), null out audit actor references and remove workspace memberships, then delete the GoTrue user and every linked identity.

**`deleted: false` is not an error.** It means the caller is the sole active owner of at least one workspace; `blockers` is that same list. Transfer ownership of each, then retry — this is the same treatment `GET /api/v1/me`'s `sole_owner_workspaces` already gets, now the thing that actually enforces it.

No rollback: a failure between the two write steps leaves the account partially prepared, the same gap the internal route this replaces already had.

**Session bearers only.** An API key is minted for exactly one profile — it is not a person, has no sessions and no linked identities — so this route answers `403 insufficient_scope` for one. Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses).

403.description: The credential is an API key (single-profile by design)

delete.description:
Revokes every session the caller holds EXCEPT the one this request was made with — which is identified from the bearer token's own `session_id` claim, so a client cannot accidentally sign itself out and cannot ask to keep a session that is not its own.

Returns what is left: the caller's remaining sessions, freshest first. That is a fact the response actually reads, unlike a bare `revoked: true` — and it saves the round trip a client would otherwise make to redraw the list.

**Session bearers only.** An API key is minted for exactly one profile — it is not a person, has no sessions and no linked identities — so this route answers `403 insufficient_scope` for one. Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses).

delete.description:
Signs one device out. The revoke is scoped to the caller's own sessions in SQL, so a session id belonging to someone else deletes nothing — and answers exactly as a session id that never existed does, so the response is not a way to test whether an id is real.

Revoking the CURRENT session is permitted and means signing yourself out; `is_current` on `GET /api/v1/me` is how a UI decides whether to offer it.

Returns the caller's remaining sessions, freshest first.

patch.description:
The ONE column the settings page's inline editor changes: which milestone (`event_key`) this CRM pipeline-stage LABEL maps to. `outcome_definitions` are NOT `conversion_definitions` — see `GET /api/v1/goals/definitions`'s description for the distinction. A definition belonging to another profile answers 404, byte-identical to one that does not exist.

**Mapping a CRM's stages (#1800).** `GET /api/v1/connections/{provider}/stages` lists every stage with its `outcome_definition_id`, the suggested outcome and the current one; write a stage's mapping here, one row per stage. Idempotent: the same `event_key` twice leaves the same row. For a `pipeline_stage` row `event_key` must be one of that read's `outcomes[].key` (otherwise 422); the edit applies to what ingestion reads from now on.

404.description: The definition does not exist, or belongs to another profile

409.description: `entitlement_required` — the profile was provisioned by an app and does not have the `atribu_attribution` entitlement; the app enables it with `PUT /api/v1/profiles/{profileId}/entitlements/atribu_attribution`. `GET /api/v1/connections/{provider}/stages` reports this up front as `write_blocked_reason: "entitlement_required"`.

422.description: `validation_error` — a missing/malformed field, or (for a `pipeline_stage` definition) an `event_key` outside the pipeline-stage vocabulary: lead_created, contacted, follow_up, appointment_booked, no_show, showed, qualified, disqualified, closed_lost, closed_won, ignored.

put.summary: Replace one family of outcome definitions
put.description:
Delete-then-insert every `outcome_definitions` row of ONE family (`pipeline_stage` | `order_event`) for this profile, replacing it with the given list. This is the shape onboarding's finish/skip step and the settings page's mode-switch seeding both use to (re)write a whole pipeline-stage or order-event ladder at once — there is no per-row create; use this with the family's full desired list, including rows that are not changing.

For `pipeline_stage`, every `event_key` must be in the same vocabulary `PATCH /api/v1/outcome-definitions/{id}` enforces (422 otherwise, before anything is deleted). A partner mapping a CRM's stages should NOT use this route: it re-inserts the family with new ids and without the CRM stage ids — PATCH each stage instead.

NOT wrapped in a database transaction: a failure between the delete and the insert can leave the family empty. The browser code this route replaces was not atomic either (two sequential calls with no rollback), so this is not a regression.

409.description: `entitlement_required` — the profile was provisioned by an app and does not have the `atribu_attribution` entitlement; the app enables it with `PUT /api/v1/profiles/{profileId}/entitlements/atribu_attribution`. `GET /api/v1/connections/{provider}/stages` reports this up front as `write_blocked_reason: "entitlement_required"`.

422.description: `validation_error` — a missing/malformed field, or (for a `pipeline_stage` definition) an `event_key` outside the pipeline-stage vocabulary: lead_created, contacted, follow_up, appointment_booked, no_show, showed, qualified, disqualified, closed_lost, closed_won, ignored.

post.summary: Propose a Meta Custom Audience stack
post.description:
Computes the seed and records the proposal. **Nothing is uploaded to Meta here** — `/audiences/confirm` is the consent moment, and every response says so in `consent_note`.

`value_lookalike` (the default) builds a value-based seed plus a 1% and a 1–5% lookalike, and refuses with 422 below Meta's 100-member floor. `exclusion` and `retargeting` are identity-only cohorts: one row, no lookalike children, and **no floor** — excluding even a handful of buyers is the point of an exclusion audience.

refundsSubtracted.description: Refunded cash removed from the seed values, as a positive amount.

leadCustomers.description: Qualified leads available for the identity-only fallback seed.

lookalikes.description: The proposed lookalike ladder (1% and a 1–5% BAND, not a second overlapping 5%).

consent_note.description: Always present, because the separation it describes is the feature: proposing computes the seed and records the proposal, and NOTHING reaches Meta until `/audiences/confirm`.

post.summary: Point ad sets at this rule's conversion event
post.description:
Re-points up to 20 ad sets' `promoted_object` at the event this rule sends, one at a time so a single failure cannot cancel the rest. Every write goes through the Meta action layer, so each one has an audit row, an idempotent replay key and a rollback.

Compatibility is re-checked first (#2145): if any requested ad set's campaign objective cannot optimize for the rule's event (Meta's objective × event table, the same verdict `GET /api/v1/conversion-sync/wiring/campaigns` reports as `incompatible`), the whole request answers `422 validation_error` naming those ad sets, and nothing is written.

Ad sets Meta froze at publish come back in `needs_duplicate_swap` untouched. Re-sending with `confirm_duplicate_swap: true` and a `duplicate_swap_mode` QUEUES their rebuild as one background job per ad set (#2143) and answers at once with `queued` and `operation`; follow it at `GET /api/v1/conversion-sync/operations/{id}`. `switch` pauses the original once the replacement is live, `run_both` leaves both running. There is deliberately NO default — one pauses a running ad set and the other doubles the money on that audience.

**Partners (#306 option B).** An API key or MCP user token that sends `confirm_duplicate_swap: true` must also send `consent: { version, text_hash, accepted_by, accepted_at }` for the CURRENT consent text, which your UI renders verbatim (Partners → Automated duplicate-and-swap). Missing, another version, another text or older than 24 hours → `409 consent_required` with `error.consent` naming the current version and hashes; nothing is read from or sent to Meta. Every rebuild is stated in `warnings` (new ad set ids, learning reset, double spend).

Rebuilding is the only route and it costs a new ad set id, a learning reset and (in `switch` mode) a pause of the original — so it needs its own yes: re-send with `confirm_duplicate_swap` and a `duplicate_swap_mode`.

post.summary: Provision the Clean Dataset and its neutral conversions
post.description:
Creates a FRESH dataset in the profile's ad account (a Clean Dataset must have zero restriction history, so an existing one is never adopted), registers one NEUTRAL custom conversion per tracked outcome event, and persists the pair as a Platform-Safe `meta_capi` destination. Every Meta write goes through the action layer, so each one leaves an audit row and is keyed for idempotent replay — a retry after a lost response reports the dataset that exists rather than spending the account's only other pixel slot. Workspace owners and admins only when the caller is a person; an API key with `exports:write` may.

**Idempotent.** When a Clean Dataset already covers every tracked outcome type the answer is `already_provisioned`, straight from Atribu's database: no Meta call, no write. A newly tracked outcome type falls through to the full path, which resumes the same dataset and registers only the missing conversion.

**Partner order (#306).** An API key or an MCP user token must switch the profile to `platform_safe` FIRST (`PUT /api/v1/conversion-sync/catalog`) — otherwise `409 platform_safe_required`. That is also the fail-safe order: a Platform-Safe profile with no Clean Dataset sends Meta nothing. The Meta connection is the one an enabled Meta CAPI destination names, or else the profile's single connected Meta Ads account.

post.summary: Apply the Platform-Safe go-live change
post.description:
**Prefer `POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/platform-safe/go-live` (#2152)**, which moves any number of ad sets as ONE background operation with no Meta write in the request; the Atribu console no longer calls this route.

Moves the named ad sets onto the Clean Dataset — its STANDARD event (`{pixel_id, custom_event_type}`) whenever the conversion is a standard Meta event, the neutral Custom Conversion only otherwise (#1669: a Custom Conversion's rule reads a custom parameter, which Meta's Core Setup strips). Each ad set's target is recomputed SERVER-SIDE and never trusted from the body, so a stale tab cannot send an ad set somewhere unexpected. The in-place re-point is always attempted first, even when a preview said it would fail — the attempt is the authoritative test and a preview is a snapshot; only Meta's frozen-ad-set refusal escalates to a rebuild, and only with `confirm_recreate` — which QUEUES the rebuild as a background job per ad set (#2143) and answers at once with `queued` and `operation`. Rides the action layer, so every write has pre-state, an audit row and a rollback. Workspace owners and admins only when the caller is a person: this switches which event campaigns optimize on and resets Meta's learning.

**Partners (#306 option B).** An API key or MCP user token that sends `confirm_recreate: true` must also send `consent: { version, text_hash, accepted_by, accepted_at }` for the CURRENT consent text, which your UI renders verbatim (Partners → Automated duplicate-and-swap). Missing, another version, another text or older than 24 hours → `409 consent_required` with `error.consent` naming the current version and hashes; nothing is sent to Meta. Every rebuild is stated in `warnings` (new ad set ids, learning reset, double-spend window). A partner rebuild needs `platform_safe_target: clean`; under `existing` it is `409 invalid_state` naming the `switch_to_clean_dataset` remediation (`POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/platform-safe/target`).

Absent, those ad sets come back in `needs_recreate` UNTOUCHED: recreating costs a new ad set id (reporting history does not follow it) and a learning reset, so it needs its own yes, not the one given for a re-point.

post.summary: Start the Platform-Safe go-live as one background operation
post.description:
Moves the named ad sets onto the Clean Dataset as ONE background operation on the Recreate engine (#2152, ADR 0024) and answers at once. The request makes Meta READS only — the same resolution as `GET /api/v1/conversion-sync/platform-safe/repoint`, so each target is recomputed server-side and never trusted from the body. In the operation, every ad set first tries the in-place edit (same ad set, its history kept); only when Meta answers that it froze the ad set at publish (code 100 / subcode 3260011) is it recreated — and only with `confirm_recreate`. One call is one operation whatever the ad-set count; a rebuild runs per ad set with a lock, cleans up its own copy on failure, and waits out Meta's rate limits for minutes when it has to.

Prefer this over `POST …/platform-safe/repoint`, which edits in the request at most 20 ad sets per call.

Workspace owners and admins only when the caller is a person. **Partners (#306 option B):** `confirm_recreate: true` from an API key or MCP user token needs `consent` for the current consent text, and `platform_safe_target: clean`.

ad_set_ids.description: Every ad set to move, in ONE call — usually the preview's `affected` rows that are not `blocked`. Nothing Meta-facing runs in the request, so there is no per-call latency budget; the 500 cap only bounds one operation.

confirm_recreate.description: Consent to REBUILD the ad sets Meta froze at publish (new ad set id, learning reset, the original paused last). Without it every ad set Meta allows is still edited in place, and a frozen one fails in the operation as `needs_recreate_consent` with nothing built.

allOf.description: #306 — REQUIRED for an API key or MCP user token when `confirm_recreate` is true. Missing or stale → `409 consent_required`, checked before any Meta call. Ignored for a session.

queued_count.description: Ad sets queued in this operation.

operation.description: The ONE background operation this go-live runs as. Progress per ad set — edited in place (`outcome: repointed`), recreated, or failed with its reason — at `GET /api/v1/conversion-sync/operations/{operation_id}`.

skipped.description: Requested ad sets that were NOT queued. `not_offered` — not a live conversion ad set still off the Clean Dataset (already on it, already replaced, or unknown to the ad account). `unmappable` — the Clean Dataset has no conversion for its event.

403.description: Missing the required scope, or (on the write) not a workspace owner/admin

409.description: `consent_required` — a key or MCP token confirmed rebuilds without a current consent. `invalid_state` — no Clean Dataset yet, none of the requested ad sets can be moved, a go-live is already running on the profile, or a partner confirmed rebuilds while `platform_safe_target` is `existing`.

consent.description: Present on `consent_required`: the current consent version and text hashes.

post.summary: Switch where the Platform-Safe feed goes: existing dataset or Clean Dataset
post.description:
Platform-Safe scrubs every Meta event the same way (default-deny `custom_data`, origin-only URL, neutral names); `platform_safe_target` decides WHICH dataset receives them (#1669).

`existing` (the default) sends to the profile's ordinary Meta CAPI destination(s) — the dataset its live ad sets already optimize on, so nothing is recreated. Meta classifies a data SOURCE (domain + business), not single events, so the scrubbed feed adds nothing a restriction reacts to.

`clean` is the remediation once Meta restricts that dataset (Events Manager shows Lead / Schedule / Purchase blocked). It runs the provision (idempotent), flips the target ONLY when a Clean Dataset exists afterwards, and lists the ad sets to recreate on it — move them with `POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/platform-safe/go-live` (one background operation). When the provision answers `action_required`, the target stays `existing` (`switched: false`) so the profile keeps sending rather than sending nothing.

Back to `existing` is refused with `409 clean_dataset_has_live_ad_sets` while ad sets on the Clean Dataset are still delivering (or when Meta cannot be read to check), unless `confirm_live_ad_sets: true`.

Only on a profile in `platform_safe` mode. Workspace owners and admins only when the caller is a person; an API key with `exports:write` may.

post.description: `multipart/form-data`: `document_name` (required), `document_type`, and a `file` and/or an `external_url` — at least one, because a row with neither records nothing a reader can open. Files are capped at 10 MB and must be PDF, PNG, JPEG, DOC or DOCX; `external_url` must be https. Workspace owners and admins only when the caller is a person.

post.summary: Re-queue failed, dead-lettered or skipped conversion exports
post.description:
Resets matching `conversion_exports` rows to `pending` and hands the worker a job.

The profile's legal gate is checked FIRST and refuses with 409 when it blocks — the worker re-checks per candidate, but resetting rows that will only be re-skipped burns their retry budget and reports a replay that will never send. Only enabled destinations are targeted, for the same reason. If the enqueue then fails, the rows are put back to `failed`: a `pending` row with no job is one nothing will ever pick up.

post.summary: Revive a setup link after a partial Meta permission grant
post.description:
Pushes the expiry window out and stamps `fix_requested_at`. **The URL does not change**, so neither does the hand-off handle — its clock is renewed alongside the link's, because a hand-off reporting `expired` for a link the human can still open is exactly the divergence one object was meant to end. Meta re-asks the declined permissions on the next OAuth because the start route always sets `auth_type=rerequest`.

Refuses an API key, for the same reason as the create.

handoff_id.description: The `pick` hand-off minted BESIDE the link, so an agent that cannot open a browser has one id to poll via `GET /api/v1/handoffs/{id}`. Its clock mirrors the link's (14 days), not the hand-off default. NULL when the mint failed — the link is what the human needs, and losing the agent's poll handle never costs the agency the link.

post.summary: Re-send recent conversions with the enriched match-quality payload
post.description:
The one-click implement: re-queues up to 500 of the destination's sent conversions from the last 30 days so they ship with every identifier Atribu can now supply.

Safe on Meta's side — every event carries an `event_id`, so Meta deduplicates the re-send against the original rather than double-counting, and EMQ recalculates in near-real-time. 202: the work is handed to the worker, not done in the request.

get.summary: Reconcile a Meta dataset against what Atribu sends
get.description:
The Events Manager Overview table rendered inside Atribu: every event on the dataset with its total volume, how many of those Atribu sent, how many ad sets optimize for it, and its EMQ.

**The point is the events Atribu did NOT send.** A dataset fed by another Conversions API source, used by twenty ad sets, that Atribu has never sent once, used to be invisible here while the rules page said "no ad sets optimizing" — true of Atribu's own conversions — and a customer read the two as contradicting.

The event list is the UNION of the three name sources, never an intersection: a lagging source must not hide the disagreement this table exists to explain.

post.summary: Create the WhatsApp or Instagram dataset, or attach an existing website pixel (idempotent)
post.description: Creates the Meta dataset linked to the profile's WhatsApp Business Account (or fetches the one Meta already has), grants Atribu's system user access, and wires it as an ENABLED Conversions API destination whose `export_from` is now — history is never sent. `201` when this call created the destination, `200` when it already existed (a retry is safe). For a profile a consumer app provisioned this is the ONLY way the dataset gets created; connecting WhatsApp or Meta Ads only reports `ready`. A delegated key may call it only for a profile its own app provisioned; a person must be a workspace owner or admin. `website`: body `{ dataset_id }` — one of the connected ad account's EXISTING pixels (`selectable_pixels`); validated against Meta's listing, wired as the website destination with `export_from` = now. Atribu NEVER creates a pixel here. The same pixel again is 200; a different pixel while one is attached is 409. `instagram` (2026-10-07): exactly like `whatsapp`, on the profile's connected Instagram professional account (`POST /{ig_user_id}/dataset` at Meta); no body. Events that carry the Instagram messaging identity (`click_ids.messaging_channel: instagram` + `click_ids.ig_sid` + `click_ids.instagram_business_account_id`) are then exported to it as `business_messaging`. Meta requires the app's advanced `instagram_manage_events` access; without it Meta refuses and the call answers with Meta's classified error.

post.summary: Build a campaign blueprint tree
post.description:
Creates a Testing campaign of 1-4 cells plus a CBO Winners campaign, optionally with a retargeting branch, and copies the chosen ads into each cell.

**The refusals are the product.** Seven preflights run BEFORE the first of ~30 Meta writes: an interest-only tree has no control; a budget that cannot feed the chosen event will spend money and learn nothing; more cells than the budget supports starve each below Meta's ~50-event learning threshold; an event that has not fired in 7 days is not wired; an archived ad cannot be copied; a pixel different from the account's live ad sets needs an explicit acknowledgement. Each answers **200** with `outcome: "refused"` and a message — a refusal guarantees nothing was created.

`idempotency_key` is required and replay-safe: a retry whose response was lost reports the tree that exists (`outcome: "replayed"`) rather than re-running the refusals against an account that already has it.

target_cpa_minor.description: Used ONLY when the event has no observed CPA — an observed CPA is a measurement, a target is a hope.

refusal.description: Present on `refused`. A refusal is a considered product answer with a payload the caller renders (the assessment drives "run one cell instead"), which is why it is a 200 and not a 4xx — and why it guarantees NOTHING was created.

post.summary: Graduate a winning Testing cell into the Winners campaign
post.description:
Copies the cell's winning ADS into the CBO Winners ad set (never the ad set itself — Meta freezes `promoted_object` at publish), pauses the source cell, and raises the Winners budget by at most +25%.

**The +25% cap is learning-phase arithmetic, not caution:** a bigger jump re-enters the learning phase and discards exactly the delivery history the graduation was earned with.

**Refuses an API key (403).** This is the one operation on the surface at tier `money` — activating Winners is the moment real spend starts, and Atribu's action executor requires a human on the record before it will move money. Use a signed-in session or an MCP user token.

post.summary: Let the daily pass graduate this blueprint's cells
post.description:
Turning this ON lets the daily graduation pass run the promotion itself instead of only proposing it.

**Enabling refuses an API key (403); disabling does not.** The row records the person answerable for every automated promotion the blueprint makes afterwards, and that id is exactly what the pass later hands the `money`-tier gate. A key would arm the switch with no one on record, the blueprint would read as auto-graduating, and every promotion would then be silently refused. Disarming needs no human.

get.summary: Budget-scaling guidance for every active ad set
get.description:
A per-ad-set directional call from the traceable-ROAS trend, an early-stage Cox fatigue signal and an instrumentation-health gate. No new attribution math — the guidance is the shared `deriveScaleGuidance`.

**The fatigue leg is directional, not validated.** The deployed Cox models carry no held-out cross-validation, so a `fatiguing` direction is a hint to look, not a proven verdict. Weight it accordingly, and do not present it to an end user as validated.

**Budgets are MINOR units.** Read them with `minor_per_major`; a hardcoded `/100` is wrong by two orders of magnitude for every whole-unit currency. When `currency_unavailable` is true the unit is unknown and no symbol should be printed.

schema.description: Attribution model for the ROAS trend. Defaults to `last_touch`.

parameters.description: Attribution model for the ROAS trend. Defaults to `last_touch`.
parameters.name: model

200.description: Ranked ad sets, actionable directions first

currency.description: The ad account's own currency, read live from Meta. NULL means the read FAILED — it is never guessed. See `currency_unavailable`.

currency_unavailable.description: True ⇒ the currency read failed, so `currency` and `minor_per_major` are null and every budget below is in an UNKNOWN unit. A renderer must say "couldn't check" rather than pick a symbol — printing dollars for pesos is a 100x misstatement on a screen that carries a one-click budget change.

minor_per_major.description: How many minor units make a major one in `currency`. 1 for whole-unit currencies (CLP, COP, CRC, HUF, IDR, ISK, …) where Meta's minor unit IS the major unit.

fatigue_unavailable.description: True ⇒ the Cox fatigue read FAILED, so every `fatigue` below is null for that reason rather than because nothing is fatiguing. Fatigue is the one signal that OVERRIDES a `room_to_scale` verdict, so this is the difference between "safe to scale" and "we could not check whether this ad is dying".

daily_budget_minor.description: MINOR units per day, verbatim from Meta — divide by `minor_per_major`, never by a hardcoded 100. Null when the campaign owns the budget (CBO) or the ad set is on a lifetime budget.

is_directional.description: Always `true`. A structural reminder that this is a DIRECTIONAL read of traceable ROAS and fatigue — never a causal or incrementality claim. Consumers must label it as such.

rule.description: The rule behind a rule-based verdict: `id` (render it with its dictionary sentence), the `thresholds` it compares against, and this verdict's measured `inputs`. A rule, not a model.

guidance.description: The directional call and WHAT it was derived from. `basis` names the signals that actually contributed — read it with `fatigue_unavailable` below, because a missing signal lowers confidence rather than changing the direction.

recent_spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

A learned value. `status` = `served` (a model that cleared the out-of-time serving gate scored this row; `value` is set) | `withheld` (the model has not demonstrated skill out of time — no value, show «no evaluado», never 0) | `not_applicable` (the model serves, but not this row). Read `value` only after checking `status === 'served'`.

A learned value. `status` = `served` (a model that cleared the out-of-time serving gate scored this row; `value` is set) | `withheld` (the model has not demonstrated skill out of time — no value, show «no evaluado», never 0) | `not_applicable` (the model serves, but not this row). Read `value` only after checking `status === 'served'`.

post.summary: Undo an applied Meta action
post.description:
Restores the pre-change state recorded on the action's own log row. The token is re-resolved from the connection THAT ACTION was applied with, not the profile's current one, so an action stays undoable after the wiring moves on.

**Deliberately accepts an API key**, unlike the money-tier operations it can undo. Rolling back has no tier gate, both audit columns are nullable, and an undo an agent cannot reach is an undo that will not happen in time.

A refusal carries its REASON: `not_reversible` with a `reason_code` is a considered answer (Meta cannot be put back the way it was), which is why it is a 200 and not a 4xx. For a budget change, a pause and a resume the live object is read first: when it no longer carries what the action wrote (a later change, or a person in Ads Manager), the answer is `not_reversible` with `reason_code: "state_drifted"` and nothing is written — a rollback never restores a stale pre-state over a newer change.

The person behind a session/user token, or — for the key of the app that provisioned the profile — its shadow owner, is recorded on the rollback row. A connection whose recorded Meta grant lacks `ads_management` is `403 meta_write_permission_missing` before any Meta call.

200.description: Rolled back, not reversible, or no longer in an undoable state

reason_code.description: On `not_reversible`. "Nothing to restore" and "the change landed and Meta cannot be put back" are different claims and a caller renders them differently.

current_status.description: On `invalid_state` — what the action's status actually is (e.g. already rolled back).

get.summary: Read the Outcome Catalog: what this profile can send, by Source
get.description: The profile's outcomes (conversion definitions), each with its Sources — Web, CRM, payments, messages, derived from the ingestion path of every row in the last 30 days and from the event names that feed it — and the 7- and 30-day volume per Source. Every CRM pipeline stage is its own item, grouped by pipeline, with its enter/leave volume and the outcome it already counts as (a stage whose event key an outcome lists). Each item carries the Meta event and value a new Sync Rule would start from; an item no standard event fits carries none, only ranked suggestions. Volumes fail SOFT and visibly: a failed volume read returns null volumes and `volume_status: unavailable`, never zeros.

primary_source.description: The Source the outcome is listed under: its busiest, else its first event name's.

volume_7d.description: Null when the volume read failed (`volume_status`) — unknown, never 0.

volume_30d.description: Null when the volume read failed (`volume_status`) — unknown, never 0.

sources.description: Every Source the outcome is observed in (from each row's ingestion path) or fed by (from its event names, plus `crm` when a pipeline stage counts as it), busiest first. A multi-Source outcome is ONE item with one entry per Source.

volume_7d.description: Null when the volume read failed (`volume_status`) — unknown, never 0.

volume_30d.description: Null when the volume read failed (`volume_status`) — unknown, never 0.

get.summary: Read everything the Conversion Sync setup surface renders
get.description: One request covering conversion definitions and their 7-day volumes, pipeline-stage options and theirs, every export destination with a computed readiness diagnosis, the connections behind them, the privacy settings, the legal-compliance summary, Meta's cached Dataset Quality verdicts, and webhook liveness. Volumes fail SOFT — a failed volume read reports 0 everywhere rather than failing the whole read — because they are guidance, not a gate.

attribution_eligible.description: False for a top-of-funnel definition (`view_content`, `add_to_cart`, …). Such a conversion never leaves `pending` by design, so a raw pending count is a misleading backlog proxy.

volume_7d.description: Outcome events matching this definition over the last 7 days. Guidance, never a gate: a failed volume read degrades every definition to 0 rather than failing the catalog.

tiktok_pixel_code.description: TikTok pixel code (Events API `event_source_id`). Null on every non-TikTok destination.

destination_config.description: The destination's own stored configuration — provider-shaped, including the Platform-Safe `mode`/`dataset_id`/`outcome_conversion_mappings` block when this is a Clean Dataset.

issues.description: `destination_disabled`, `missing_connection`, `connection_<status>`, `missing_meta_pixel_id`, `missing_google_conversion_action`, `missing_tiktok_pixel_code`. `destination_disabled` is excluded from the readiness test: a destination that is merely switched off is `inactive`, not misconfigured.

connections.description: Ad and CRM connections on this profile. `whatsapp` is included so a reader can say "this profile has a WABA and no WhatsApp dataset" — it is never itself offered as an export destination.

privacy_mode.description: FOUR values, matching the database's own CHECK. `platform_safe` means the profile sends Meta a deliberately narrowed payload (default-deny `custom_data`, origin-only URL, neutral names), so health or other sensitive context cannot reach the ad platform. Which dataset receives it is `platform_safe_target`.

platform_safe_target.description: #1669 — where a `platform_safe` profile's scrubbed Meta events go. `existing` (default): the profile's ordinary Meta CAPI destination(s), the dataset its live ad sets already optimize on — no new ad sets, no learning reset. `clean`: only the provisioned Clean Dataset, the remediation once Meta restricts the existing dataset. Read-only here: change it with `POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/platform-safe/target`. Ignored in every other privacy mode.

privacy_config.description: The profile's privacy filters: `url_sanitization`, `url_allowlist`, `event_blocklist_paths`, `parameter_allowlist`, `parameter_blocklist`, the `strip_*` booleans, `enable_ldu`, and `healthcare_export_allowlist`. Every field is optional and the object is validated STRICTLY on write — an unrecognized key is refused rather than dropped, because silently accepting a misspelled privacy control would report success for a filter that was never applied.

dataset_quality.description: Meta's last Dataset Quality answer per destination, straight from the `meta_dataset_quality` CACHE — never a fresh Graph call, which would put a provider round trip on every catalog load. Refresh it with `GET /api/v1/conversion-sync/dataset-quality`. An empty array means we have not asked yet, which is not the same as a healthy dataset.

put.summary: Replace the profile's privacy and export settings
put.description:
A PUT, not a PATCH: the body is the complete privacy state and the write replaces it. Only a workspace owner or admin may CHANGE `privacy_mode` — downgrading out of HIPAA or Platform-Safe silently re-leaks health context — but re-writing the SAME mode is open to any member, so editing an allowlist or an export toggle does not need an owner. An API key holding `exports:write` may do either. Returns the settings as they stand AFTER the write, not an echo of the request.

Writing `platform_safe` or `hipaa` makes the profile healthcare-family (policy S5): every live partner key on it carrying `customers:read` or `visitors:read` is revoked (#1782). A partner app can set the same mode at provisioning instead (`POST /api/v1/profiles`, `privacy_mode`).

privacy_config.description: REQUIRED, and the write REPLACES it. Send `{}` to clear every filter. It is required rather than optional because the handler this replaces defaulted an absent value to `{}` and then wrote it — so a caller that simply forgot the key erased the profile's parameter allowlist (which on a Platform-Safe profile IS its opt-in field list) and every `strip_*` flag, silently.

export_meta_enabled.description: Omitted leaves the stored value alone.

export_google_enabled.description: Omitted leaves the stored value alone.

Which dataset receives it is `platform_safe_target`.

Read-only here: change it with `POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/platform-safe/target`. Ignored in every other privacy mode.

Every field is optional and the object is validated STRICTLY on write — an unrecognized key is refused rather than dropped, because silently accepting a misspelled privacy control would report success for a filter that was never applied.

post.summary: Upload a proposed audience to Meta
post.description: THE CONSENT MOMENT. Rebuilds the seed FRESH — the customer base may have moved since the proposal, and what gets uploaded must be what is true now — then creates the value-based Custom Audience and its lookalike stack through the Meta action layer, which brings the audit row, the idempotent replay and the rollback with it. The idempotency key is the proposal's own id, so a retry after a lost response adopts the audience that already exists instead of building a second stack. Identifiers are SHA-256 hashed before they leave.

The proposal is left marked `error` with `audience_tos_required`, so the state is visible without re-calling.

post.summary: Pause, resume, or delete a managed audience

Delete removes it at Meta too, CHILDREN FIRST, because Meta refuses to delete an origin audience that still has live lookalikes hanging off it; each child that exists at Meta goes through the action layer so the delete is audited like every other write. A row that never reached Meta is marked deleted locally with no provider call at all.

It is NOT a per-profile setting: `profiles.currency` still governs every profile-grain amount, and those are never converted.

post.summary: Accept a workspace or profile invitation
post.description:
The caller must already be signed in with the SAME email the invitation was sent to (`403 forbidden` on a mismatch) — this route never creates an account; the brand-new-user path is the console's own signup flow. Idempotent membership creation: re-activates a removed/invited row rather than duplicating it, and never downgrades an existing higher-tier role. `409`/`410` on an already-accepted, revoked or expired invitation, or `410 workspace_archived` when the invitation's workspace has since been archived (terminal — not retryable).

**Session bearers only** — there is no key to present before the caller has a workspace.

200.description: The workspace (and, for a profile invite, the profile) the caller now belongs to

400.description: Missing token or invitationId

403.description: Signed in with a different email than the invitation was sent to

404.description: Invitation not found

409.description: Already accepted

410.description: Revoked, expired, or the invitation's workspace was archived (`workspace_archived`)

get.summary: Get the profile's setup checklist and the one next thing to do
get.description:
An ordered checklist of what this profile still needs before ads, outcomes and attribution work end to end — and, for each unfinished step, the one next action.

**Derived, never stored.** Every step is computed at read time from the state the rest of the product keeps: connections, tracker events, conversion definitions, attribution windows, export destinations and rules, the DPA, the plan, and whether Atribu's attribution pipeline is enabled for this profile at all. There is no checklist table and nothing here is a cached snapshot, so a connection that broke an hour ago shows as `degraded` on the next call.

**`wizard_finished` is not the answer to this question.** It is the legacy `onboarding_completed` boolean — a person pressed Finish — and every wizard step is skippable, so it is reported alongside the steps rather than folded into them.

**A partner-provisioned profile answers `attribution_enabled: blocked`, not an empty checklist.** Profiles created through a partner application deliberately do not hold the `atribu_attribution` entitlement, and Atribu's pipeline is a no-op for them — so every other step can be completed and still produce no attributed conversions. That is reported as the first step, with its reason.

Read `summary.next_step` for the single thing to do now; read `steps` to render the whole flow. This response carries no account ids, no pixel ids, no amounts and no PII.

404.description: The profile does not exist, or this caller cannot reach it

get.summary: Get the profile's attribution windows
get.description:
The four window settings that decide how far back a touch still gets credit for a conversion: `click_window_days`, `view_window_hours`, `first_touch_window_days` and `cash_window_days`. Returns the table's own defaults (30 / 24 / 90 / null) when the profile has no `profile_attribution_settings` row yet — the same behavior the console's settings page has always had.

This is a NARROW slice of that table: session timeout/mode, geo/user-agent/channel enrichment toggles and the Meta/Google export switches live on the same row but have no v1 surface yet and are not returned here.

patch.description:
A PARTIAL update over the four window columns — an omitted key is left untouched, matching `PATCH /api/v1/profile`'s convention. `cash_window_days: null` clears the override (cash conversions fall back to the normal windows); omitting it leaves the current value alone.

A window change redefines which touches attach to which conversion RETROACTIVELY, so every successful save enqueues ONE full-profile attribution replay — reported as `replay_queued` (+ `replay_error` when it could not be queued), the same non-fatal, REPORTED tail `POST /api/v1/channel-rules` uses for the identical reason. An empty body (no recognized field) is a no-op: it returns the current settings unchanged with `replay_queued: false`.

Out-of-range values answer `400 invalid_parameter` naming the field: `click_window_days` 1–365, `view_window_hours` 1–168, `first_touch_window_days` 1–365, `cash_window_days` null or 1–730.

200.description: The updated (or unchanged) settings, plus the replay outcome

400.description: A window field is out of range, or the body is malformed

get.summary: Recommend attribution windows from the profile's own sales cycle
get.description: Measures, per paying customer whose first cash payment landed in the trailing 365 days, the days from their FIRST ad touch to that payment, and recommends windows that cover it: a first-touch window covering 80% of customers (capped at 365) and a click window covering the median (capped at 90). It never recommends narrowing a window. Read-only — apply it with `PATCH /api/v1/profile/attribution-settings`, which queues the full replay.

200.description: The measured cycle and the recommendation

get.summary: List the profile's Stripe products and whether ads sell them
get.description: Every Stripe product the profile sells, with Atribu's proposal (`advertised` when sold through a Payment Link or Checkout, `unknown` otherwise), the owner's answer, and the cash and payments of the last `recent_days`. Products with no sale in `active_days` have `sold_recently: false`.

patch.summary: Answer whether ads sell a product
patch.description: Records the owner's answer for one product and re-classifies the profile's Stripe conversions at once: a payment whose products are all `not_advertised` leaves ad-attributable cash (reason `non_marketing_product`), and one that no longer qualifies comes back. When anything moved, a recompute is queued (`replay_queued`). An answer equal to the one in force is a no-op.

200.description: The product's status after the answer

400.description: A malformed product id or status

404.description: The profile has never sold or listed this product

post.summary: Create and seed this workspace's demo profile
post.description:
One call gives a workspace something to read before any live account is connected: a profile flagged `is_demo`, sixty days of a fictional clinic's Meta traffic, and a Meta CAPI destination that RECORDS what it would have sent.

**The engine runs for real.** The seed writes INPUTS — ad structure, daily spend, identities, marketing touches, and `outcome_events` through the same CRM-ingest primitive every real provider uses — then enqueues an ordinary recompute. `conversions` and `attribution_touchpoints` across all five attribution models come out of the pipeline, not out of the seed. That is why the counts below report what the recompute WILL produce: it runs asynchronously, so poll `GET /api/v1/overview`.

**What the demo is excluded from.** Its own reads show its own money — that is the point. Every read that spans the profiles of a workspace leaves it out: the pacing aggregate, Top Performers cohorts and the `creative_feature_store` rebuild, the agency Reports hub, alert digest emails, the ML ad-fact and creative-lifecycle passes, and the `active_profiles` plan limit (a demo consumes no seat, and creating one is not gated by the limit).

**Exports never leave.** See `destination.mode`.

**Idempotent.** A workspace holds at most one demo profile. Calling this again re-seeds the existing one and answers 200; only the first call answers 201.

Session bearers and user tokens only — an API key is minted for exactly one profile and belongs to no workspace, so it answers `403 insufficient_scope`.

delete.description:
Removes the demo profile and everything under it — touches, outcome events, conversions, attribution, spend, the seeded ad structure, the recording destination and its ledger — in one call.

**Delete means archive + purge, and audit rows are retained (#1170).** `conversion_exports` records what Atribu transmitted (or, for a demo, would have transmitted) on your behalf, and a database trigger refuses to let any user-facing path erase it. Those rows — and the handful their foreign keys pin in place (the exported outcome event, its customer, the destination and the rule) — stay attached to the archived profile; `retained_audit_rows` counts them. Everything else is gone.

The archived profile disappears from every read (`archived_at IS NULL` is the filter the whole product already applies) and **releases the workspace's demo slot** (`idx_profiles_one_demo_per_workspace` is partial on `archived_at IS NULL`), so `POST /api/v1/profiles/demo` succeeds immediately afterwards.

The `is_demo` predicate is inside the statement, so this can never touch a real profile.

Deleting nothing answers 200 with `deleted: false`, not 404 — a workspace with no demo profile is the state you asked for, and a retry must not look like a failure.

post.summary: Start a sync
post.description:
Queue a manual sync for this profile — one provider, or every connected provider when `provider` is omitted.

**Asynchronous.** `202` means the jobs are queued, not that data has landed; poll `GET /api/v1/connections/sync/status?provider=…` for progress, or read `GET /api/v1/connections` for `sync.last_synced_at`.

**Not keyed by connection id, on purpose.** A profile can hold several connections for one provider (several Meta ad accounts, several GoHighLevel locations), and a sync covers all of them. A route that named one id would enqueue for its siblings anyway; this one says so.

**A sync already in flight is a `409`,** not a second run: the queue holds one job per connection and a duplicate would be dropped silently.

Scope: `attribution:write` — a sync changes what the warehouse will say.

400.description: `resource` was given with a provider other than `gohighlevel`

409.description: A sync is already in progress for this connection

422.description: Unknown provider or resource, or a malformed body

get.summary: Read a provider's sync progress
get.description:
Where one provider's sync has got to on this profile. Safe to poll — the response is `Cache-Control: no-store`, and a progress bar that caches is a progress bar that stops.

**No connection is a 200,** describing a `disconnected` provider with an empty `resources` list. A 404 would make "not connected" indistinguishable from "wrong profile".

Scope: `analytics:read`.

parameters.description: Required. Which connector's progress to report.
parameters.name: provider

200.description: The provider's sync state on this profile.

400.description: `provider` missing or not a known connector

post.summary: Disconnect an integration
post.description:
Delete the connection: stop the provider's push channel, trigger the GoHighLevel Marketplace uninstall where one applies, remove the row, emit `connection.revoked` and write an audit event.

**This is not `DELETE /api/v1/connections/{id}`.** That one is a consumer app's OAuth grant SELF-revoke: it needs an API key, it cuts the keys that grant minted, and it leaves the tenant's connection in place. This one is the tenant giving up their own integration, and it removes it.

**Requires a person, or a delegated key on a profile its own app provisioned.** A signed-in session, an MCP user token, or an `attribution:write` key whose app provisioned this profile (`profiles.provisioned_by` matches the key's app) may call this. Every other API key is a 403 — including that same delegated key on a human-owned profile, or on a profile another app provisioned: deleting a customer's Meta connection is not something a delegated read should be able to do, and an app-provisioned profile is the one case with no person on Atribu's side to do it instead.

**A sync in flight is a 409.** Wait for it: the connector's rows are mid-write.

**A connection other records still depend on is a 409, with nothing changed.** The delete is checked before any provider-side step runs, so a refused disconnect never leaves the connection half torn down. Records that outlive their connection by design (calendar booking intentions) do not block it: they are kept, with the connection reference cleared.

Scope: `attribution:write`.

403.description: The credential cannot disconnect this profile's connections: a human-owned or another app's profile with an API key (use the Atribu app, or the grant self-revoke), or a direct admin key with no app at all

404.description: No such connection on this profile

409.description: A sync is in progress, or other records still depend on the connection (nothing was changed)

post.summary: Recompute attribution
post.description:
Re-run sessions → paths → attribution for this profile. Queue this after anything that changes who gets credit: a customer merge, a channel rule, an attribution-window change.

**Asynchronous.** `202` means queued; poll `GET /api/v1/profile/recompute-status`.

**It skips the freshness cadence.** Background recomputes are throttled to roughly one per profile per window; a request made here is someone waiting on an answer, so it runs at the front. It still coalesces onto a queued job, so a loop cannot outrun the cap.

Scope: `attribution:write`.

422.description: Unknown attribution model, or a malformed body

get.summary: Is a recompute still running?
get.description:
One boolean, cheap enough to poll. Pair it with `POST /api/v1/profile/recompute` and with any write that queues a recompute of its own — a merge, a channel rule — to know when the numbers you read are the new ones.

Scope: `analytics:read`.

get.summary: Read the profile's tracker and enrichment settings
get.description:
How the tracker sessionises visits and what the enrichment pipeline resolves. The four attribution WINDOW columns live on the same database row but are a different resource — `GET /api/v1/profile/attribution-settings` — because they decide who gets CREDIT, not how an event is captured.

A profile with no settings row yet gets the defaults rather than a 404.

patch.summary: Update the profile's tracker and enrichment settings
patch.description:
A PARTIAL update — an omitted key is left untouched. `export_meta_enabled` / `export_google_enabled` are not accepted: they are owned by Conversion Sync.

Every successful save enqueues ONE full-profile replay, because these settings change how past events would have been sessionised and enriched. The outcome is REPORTED (`replay_queued`, `replay_error`) rather than thrown: the settings were saved either way, and a 500 would tell you the opposite of what happened. An empty body is a no-op — current settings, `replay_queued: false`.

200.description: The updated (or unchanged) settings, plus the replay outcome

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range

get.summary: Where this profile's tracker collects
get.description: The profile's verified first-party tracking domain if it has one, else Atribu's own origin. This is the host a marketer pastes into an ad platform's allow-list, and the host the snippet from `GET /api/v1/tracking/snippet` points at for the same profile.

get.summary: The raw enriched-event feed
get.description:
Individual tracker events, newest first, for debugging an installation: what arrived, with which UTMs and click ids, and whether it carried an identity.

REQUIRES `visitors:read`, not `analytics:read`. `payload` is the event's own body verbatim, and a `lead_submitted` payload carries the email/phone the tracker captured — so this is the PII tier, the same one `GET /api/v1/visitors` sits on.

Reads the Ephemeral Buffer, whose retention is 30 days. A longer `days` is CLAMPED, and the applied window comes back in `window.days` so a caller never attributes 30 days of numbers to the 90 it asked for. Page with `before` = the previous response's `pagination.next_cursor`.

schema.description: Look-back window. CLAMPED to the Ephemeral Buffer's retention (30 days) — the applied value is echoed back in `window.days`, never silently substituted.

parameters.description: Look-back window. CLAMPED to the Ephemeral Buffer's retention (30 days) — the applied value is echoed back in `window.days`, never silently substituted.
parameters.name: days

schema.description: Keyset cursor — pass the previous page's `pagination.next_cursor`.

parameters.description: Keyset cursor — pass the previous page's `pagination.next_cursor`.

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range

get.summary: The profile's most recent attribution replay
get.description: The latest `full_replay` run and its steps, so a client can show progress while attribution is being recalculated. `data` is `null` when the profile has never been replayed — a 200 with no run, not a 404: 'nothing is running' is an answer.

get.summary: The latest install-verification attempt
get.description: Poll this after `POST /api/v1/tracking/verification` to see whether the tracker on the customer's site has echoed the nonce back. `data` is `null` when no attempt was ever started.

post.summary: Start an install verification
post.description: Mints a nonce valid for 15 minutes. Load any tracked page with `?atb_verify=<nonce>` appended; the installed tracker posts it back and the attempt flips to `verified`, recording the URL and User-Agent it was seen on. This is the only proof that the snippet is actually live on the page the marketer thinks it is.

delete.description:
Marks the key revoked. Events sent with it after this stop being accepted, so a site still carrying it goes dark.

REFUSES (400) on the profile's LAST active key: the tracker authenticates with it, so revoking the only one would silently stop every event the site sends. Issue a replacement first with `POST /api/v1/tracking/keys` and `force_new: true`, deploy it, then revoke the old one. A key belonging to another profile answers 404, never 403 — a caller must not be able to probe which key ids exist. Revoking an already-revoked key is idempotent.

400.description: This is the profile's last active tracking key

404.description: No such key on this profile

get.summary: Warehouse diagnostics for the profile
get.description: What the ingestion and enrichment pipeline REJECTED or repaired over the window: malformed events, enrichment-stage failures, identity reassignments, and the analytics runs (plus their steps) that processed them. This is the read that answers 'my numbers look wrong — did something fail?'.

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range

get.summary: Is this profile's tracking healthy?
get.description:
Rates and counts describing the SETUP, not the people: how many events arrived, how many carried a click id, how often `identify()` fired, and whether the Meta bridge and the CAPI export are actually working.

TWO NUMBERS THAT LOOK LIKE ONE, deliberately kept apart. `summary.conversion_events` counts the TRACKER's conversion events; `business_conversions` counts the profile's conversions (the `/overview` count) over the same number of days. A profile whose sales close in a CRM will show a large gap, and that gap is the honest answer rather than a fault.

`diagnostics.meta_exports.sent` is a count over a bounded SAMPLE — read it with `sampled_conversions` and `complete`. Reads the Ephemeral Buffer, so `days` is clamped to its 30-day retention and the applied window is echoed in `window.days`.

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range

get.summary: List the profile's first-party tracking domains
get.description:
A custom domain makes tracking FIRST-PARTY. Collection through `atribu.app` is a third-party request, which ad blockers and browser privacy lists drop outright — those visitors are not degraded, they are absent. `trk.yourstore.com` gets through.

`cname_target` is what every domain here must point at.

200.description: The profile's domains and the CNAME target

post.summary: Register a first-party tracking domain
post.description:
Records the domain as `pending` and returns the CNAME to create. Nothing collects on it until `POST /api/v1/tracking/custom-domains/{id}/verify` confirms the DNS.

Idempotent on `(profile, domain)`: re-registering the same host returns the same row. Answers 503 when the deployment has no collect host configured — a domain with no CNAME target could never verify, so it is refused rather than stored.

201.description: The domain, and the DNS steps to complete

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range

503.description: No collect host is configured on this deployment

post.summary: Re-check a domain's DNS and store the verdict
post.description:
Resolves the domain and records whether it points at `expected_cname`. Passes on a matching CNAME **or** an IP overlap — a Cloudflare-proxied domain has its CNAME flattened to A/AAAA records, so a correct setup often has no CNAME to read.

`verified: false` is a 200. It is a successful answer to "does this resolve yet?", which is what a client polling while the customer edits DNS needs.

200.description: The verdict, now stored on the domain

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range

404.description: No such domain on this profile

delete.description: Snippets generated afterwards fall back to the next verified domain, or to Atribu's own origin. A site still carrying the removed host in an already-deployed snippet keeps sending to a hostname nothing answers, so regenerate the snippet before removing.

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range

404.description: No such domain on this profile

get.summary: The delivery ledger, with the conversion each row carries
get.description:
The operational view of `conversion_exports`: every attempted delivery over the window, joined to the outcome event it was for.

NOT the same as `GET /api/v1/exports/ledger`, which is the PII-free external view of the same table. This one hydrates the linked conversion (its type, time and amount) because the question it answers is "which SALE failed to reach Meta", not "how many deliveries were there".

parameters.description: YYYY-MM-DD, on `conversion_exports.created_at`.
parameters.name: date_from

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range

Resets failed / dead-letter rows to `pending` and enqueues ONE dispatch job.
