put.description:
Explicit, idempotent, audited: the app that provisioned this profile turns Atribu's own pipeline on or off for it (ADR 0021).

**HTTP Basic app credentials only** — the same `client_id:client_secret` pair `POST /api/v1/profiles` uses. Never a session bearer and never an `atb_live_` key: an entitlement is a fact about your relationship with your own dealer, not something a profile-scoped analytics key should be able to change.

**Which profiles.** Only ones THIS APP provisioned — the profile must carry `provisioned_by = <your client_id>` and be unarchived, which is exactly what `POST /api/v1/profiles` writes for every dealer. Any other profile — unknown, another app's, or archived — answers `404 not_found`, identically: the response never confirms a profile id exists or which app owns it.

**Turning it ON** starts what a human-entitled profile gets: the ad-platform sync's performance-shaped work resumes, and the standard backfill window is enqueued immediately for every ad-platform connection this profile already holds — you do not need to also call `POST /api/v1/connections/sync`.

**Turning it OFF** returns the profile to connectivity-only mode: campaign/ad structure and conversational configuration (the CTWA ad greeting) keep syncing nightly, but insights/spend, messaging metrics, attribution, conversions and exports stop. No data is deleted.

**Idempotent.** Calling this again with the same `enabled` value is a no-op on the entitlement itself — HTTP 200, `changed: false`, no second audit event, and no second sync: the backfill fires once, on the real transition, so a duplicate delivery costs nothing. (If a call flipped the entitlement and then failed before the backfill was enqueued, re-arm it with `POST /api/v1/connections/sync`.) Your grant is the one thing that converges on EVERY call, replay included — see `grant`.

**Ordered, if you ask for it.** Idempotency cannot decide between two CONTRADICTORY deliveries, so an at-least-once outbox can land a retried cancellation after the renewal that replaced it. Send `occurred_at` (the subscription event's own timestamp) and Atribu discards any delivery strictly older than the newest one it has seen, answering `200` with `ignored_stale: true` and writing nothing.

**A revoked delegation is never resurrected.** If the workspace owner disconnected your app on this profile, this call still records the entitlement but leaves the grant alone and answers `grant.revoked: true`. Re-consent through `POST /api/v1/profiles`.

**The entitlement sets your grant (#1455).** Dealers never pick scopes: your app provisions a profile with the core `connections` bundle, and Atribu itself widens the profile-level grant to `["connections", "attribution"]` when you turn this entitlement ON. Turning it OFF narrows the same grant back to `["connections"]` and revokes every API key minted under the wider one — within ~10 seconds, those keys answer 401. The grant is never revoked, so the connect rail never goes down with the Add-on. Only `attribution` is ever taken away: a grant that never carried it (an older delegation, say `["analytics", "attribution_write"]`) is untouched, keys included.

**Both directions need the same follow-up, and neither returns a secret:** mint a fresh key with `grant_type=client_credentials` against the same grant and swap it in. Scopes are frozen into a key at mint time, so after ON an existing key does not gain the new ones, and after OFF it is already dead; the key you mint after OFF carries `connections:read` / `connections:write` and nothing else.

**The Add-on gate.** While this entitlement is OFF, the attribution WRITE surface on this profile answers `409 entitlement_required` for every caller — `POST /api/v1/events`, the Conversion Sync writes, goals, tracking, reports, recompute, recommendation apply and creative analysis. Reads are unaffected, and so is the connect rail: connecting, syncing and disconnecting an ad account or a channel never require the Add-on.

Every real change writes an audit event naming this app, the direction, and the scope change it made.

post.summary: Pause one ad
post.description:
Pauses one ACTIVE ad by its Meta id — with no recommendation behind it. The same action-layer write `pause_underperformer` applies (tier `confirm`: this POST is the confirmation and no person is required), with the same audit trail (`meta_action_log`) and the same rollback.

Refused BEFORE any Meta call when the ad is not this profile's (`404`), the profile has no usable Meta Ads connection (`409 meta_connection_required`) or the connection's recorded grant lacks `ads_management` (`403 meta_write_permission_missing`). Pausing an already paused ad is a `200` with `outcome: "no_change"` and no Meta write; an ARCHIVED or DELETED ad is `409 invalid_state` and is never written (Meta would un-archive it).

**Undo** with `POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/actions/{action_id}/rollback` or the resume route. A rollback restores this row's PRE-STATE, and only while the ad still carries what this call wrote — if it was changed since, the rollback answers `not_reversible` with `reason_code: "state_drifted"` and writes nothing.

post.summary: Change one ad set's daily or lifetime budget
post.description:
Sets one ad set's daily budget — or its lifetime budget, with `new_lifetime_budget_minor` — by its Meta id, through the same action-layer write `scale_winner` applies. Tier `money`: a person must be on the record — send `applied_by`, use a session or MCP user token, or call with a key of the app that provisioned this profile (its shadow owner is used). Anything else is `403` before anything is read.

**The guardrail is ±50 % of the LIVE budget per call** (read from Meta at apply time, never from a snapshot), with a minimum daily budget; a change outside it is `422 budget_change_out_of_bounds`, audited as a failed row, and never reaches Meta. An ad set whose campaign owns the budget (Advantage campaign budget — use `POST /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/budget`) or that runs on the other budget type is `409 invalid_state`. An ARCHIVED or DELETED ad set, or one whose campaign is, is `409 adset_not_editable` (status read live from Meta) and nothing is written.

**Minimum budget:** Atribu refuses below its own floor of 100 minor units (`budget_change_out_of_bounds`). Meta's real per-account minimum is higher in most currencies (in CLP, ~1 000 pesos) and Atribu does not read it, so a budget between the two is attempted and Meta's refusal comes back as `422 validation_error` with Meta's own message (audited as a failed row).

**Undo** with `POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/actions/{action_id}/rollback`. It restores this row's PRE-STATE, and only while the ad set still carries the budget this call set: after a later change (yours or a person's in Ads Manager) it answers `not_reversible` with `reason_code: "state_drifted"` — roll back the latest change instead.

Unlike `POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/scaling/apply`, which keeps refusing API keys, this is the partner path.

get.summary: Get the visitor timeline behind one conversion
get.description:
The same page `GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/journey` returns — every touch and outcome, oldest first, with the credit overlay under `model` — addressed by a CONVERSION instead of a visitor. `meta.conversion` names what the handle resolved to, including the `customer_profile_id`, so a caller that started from its own event id needs no second call.

The visitor is resolved at request time: a conversion ingested anonymously and stitched to a customer since follows the customer.

**The scope decides the shape.** `conversions:read` opens the read (so does `customers:read` alone).

- **With `customers:read`**: `JourneyEvent` rows and the `meta.conversion` above (`customer_profile_id`, `anonymous_id`). A conversion with no identity at all is `409 invalid_state`.
- **Without it** — every key of a healthcare-family profile: `JourneyEventProjected` rows, the marketing path only (touch, channel, campaign / ad set / ad, click-id kind, join method, credit). The person, the pages, device, geo, session, `anonymous_id` and `customer_profile_id` are absent. `meta.conversion` carries `customer_key` — your own customer id — instead. A conversion with no identity answers `200` with no rows and `customer_key: null`.

get.summary: Get a campaign's live status and what pausing or resuming it would do
get.description:
Everything a pause/resume consent screen renders, in one call: the campaign's name, its live configured and effective status, how many ads a pause would stop (or a resume would free), its daily budget, its mean daily spend over the last complete days, and — per action — whether it is available and, if not, a `reason`.

Never a dead end for a campaign of this profile: a missing connection, a dead token or a Meta outage answers `200` with `status_source: "synced"`, Atribu's last synced status, and both actions unavailable with the reason. Three Meta reads in parallel under one ~5 s deadline (a count that does not answer is `null`, the status stays live); no write, ever.

schema.description: Meta's campaign id — the `platform_id` of a `GET /api/v1/campaigns` row. Never an internal uuid.

parameters.description: Meta's campaign id — the `platform_id` of a `GET /api/v1/campaigns` row. Never an internal uuid.
parameters.name: id

200.description: The campaign's status and the two actions' availability

status.description: Configured status: ACTIVE | PAUSED | ARCHIVED | DELETED.

effective_status.description: Meta's delivery verdict (ACTIVE, PAUSED, IN_PROCESS, WITH_ISSUES, …). Null when Meta could not be read (`status_source: "synced"`).

status_source.description: `live` — read from Meta just now. `synced` — Meta was not readable (no connection, dead token, outage); `status` is Atribu's last sync and both actions are unavailable with a `reason`.

delivering_ads_count.description: Ads a pause would stop right now (delivering, or in processing / review / with issues) — the «detiene n anuncios» number. 0 while the campaign is paused; null when unknown.

daily_budget_minor.description: The campaign's own daily budget in the ad account's MINOR units (divide by `minor_per_major`). Null when the budgets live on the ad sets.

lifetime_budget_minor.description: The campaign's own LIFETIME budget in MINOR units (divide by `minor_per_major`), when it runs on one — then `daily_budget_minor` is null and `budget_level` is `campaign`. Null for a daily-budget or ad-set-budget campaign.

minor_per_major.description: Minor units per major unit for `currency` (1 for CLP, 100 for USD).

budget_level.description: `campaign` — Advantage campaign budget. `ad_set` — each ad set carries its own.

avg_daily_spend.description: Mean daily spend over the last `spend_window_days` complete days, in `currency` MAJOR units, as an exact decimal string — the "~$X al día" a pause would stop. Null when nothing was spent.

spend_window_days.description: The complete days `avg_daily_spend` was divided by: 7, or fewer for a campaign whose first spend is more recent (a campaign launched 2 days ago is averaged over 2).

reason.description: Why not, when `available` is false: the campaign is already in that state (`already_paused` / `already_active`), ARCHIVED/DELETED (`campaign_not_pausable` / `campaign_not_resumable`), or Atribu cannot write for the advertiser (`meta_connection_missing`, `ads_management_not_granted`, `meta_reconnect_required`, `meta_unavailable`). Null when available.

affected_ads_count.description: How many ads this action would stop (pause: delivering, or in processing / review / with issues) or free (resume: held by the campaign pause, `CAMPAIGN_PAUSED`). Null when unknown — a count Meta did not answer in time is null while the status stays live. Caveat: Meta does not document whether a DISAPPROVED ad under a paused campaign reports `CAMPAIGN_PAUSED`; if it does, the resume count includes ads that will not deliver.

reason.description: Why not, when `available` is false: the campaign is already in that state (`already_paused` / `already_active`), ARCHIVED/DELETED (`campaign_not_pausable` / `campaign_not_resumable`), or Atribu cannot write for the advertiser (`meta_connection_missing`, `ads_management_not_granted`, `meta_reconnect_required`, `meta_unavailable`). Null when available.

affected_ads_count.description: How many ads this action would stop (pause: delivering, or in processing / review / with issues) or free (resume: held by the campaign pause, `CAMPAIGN_PAUSED`). Null when unknown — a count Meta did not answer in time is null while the status stays live. Caveat: Meta does not document whether a DISAPPROVED ad under a paused campaign reports `CAMPAIGN_PAUSED`; if it does, the resume count includes ads that will not deliver.

post.summary: Pause one campaign
post.description:
Pauses one ACTIVE campaign by its Meta id in ONE atomic write — the campaign's own `status`, never a fan-out over its ads. Tier `confirm` (this POST is the confirmation; no person is required), audited on `meta_action_log` with the pre-state a rollback needs. `affected_ads_count` is how many ads were delivering and stopped.

Refused BEFORE any Meta write when the campaign is not this profile's (`404`), the profile has no usable Meta Ads connection (`409 meta_connection_required`) or the connection's grant lacks `ads_management` (`403 meta_write_permission_missing`). Pausing a paused campaign is a `200` with `outcome: "no_change"` and no write; an ARCHIVED or DELETED campaign is `409 campaign_not_pausable` and is never written (Meta would un-archive it). A newer pause supersedes older ones, so a resume always undoes the newest.

**Undo** with `undo` (`POST /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/resume`). Render the consent screen from `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/status` first.

post.summary: Resume one paused campaign
post.description:
Resumes one PAUSED campaign by its Meta id in ONE write. When Atribu paused it, the resume IS that pause's undo: the new ledger row carries `rollback_of = <pause action_id>` and the pause row becomes `rolled_back`. The pause row is claimed atomically: of two concurrent resumes only one undoes it; the other re-reads the live status and answers from it (`no_change` once the campaign is active, or it resumes it itself if the first write failed). A campaign paused outside Atribu is resumed as a plain `campaign_resume`.

**Ads paused on their own stay paused.** Only the campaign's status is written, so an ad (or ad set) that was paused before the campaign pause does not come back — Meta's own semantics. `affected_ads_count` counts the ads the campaign pause was holding (`effective_status = CAMPAIGN_PAUSED`).

Resuming an active campaign is a `200` with `outcome: "no_change"` and no write, like the pause of a paused one; an ARCHIVED or DELETED campaign is `409 campaign_not_resumable`. Delivery resumes at the campaign's existing budgets.

post.summary: Raise or lower one campaign's budget
post.description:
Sets the DAILY or LIFETIME budget of one campaign whose budget lives on the campaign (Advantage campaign budget), by its Meta id, in ONE write — the campaign twin of `POST /api/v1/adsets/{id}/budget`, on the same action layer. Tier `money`: a person must be on the record — send `applied_by`, use a session or MCP user token, or call with a key of the app that provisioned this profile (its shadow owner is used). Anything else is `403` before anything is read. Audited on `meta_action_log` with the pre-state a rollback needs.

**The guardrail is ±50 % of the LIVE budget per call** (read from Meta at apply time), with a floor of 100 minor units; outside it is `422 budget_change_out_of_bounds`, audited, and never reaches Meta. A campaign with no budget of the requested type — its ad sets own the budget, or it runs on the other type — is `409 invalid_state` and nothing is written (Atribu never converts an ad-set-budget campaign into a campaign-budget one). An ARCHIVED or DELETED campaign is `409 campaign_not_editable`. Meta's own per-account minimum, and for a lifetime budget the amount already spent, are Meta's to enforce: its refusal comes back as `422` with `reason: meta_refused`.

Render the consent screen from `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}/status` (its `daily_budget_minor` / `lifetime_budget_minor` / `budget_level`).

**Undo** with `POST /api/v1/conversion-sync/actions/{action_id}/rollback`: it restores this row's PRE-STATE, and only while the campaign still carries the budget this call set (`not_reversible` / `state_drifted` after a later change).

get.description:
One row per Instagram or Facebook post published in the window, with its engagement primitives and the conversions and cash revenue Atribu credits to it.

`attributed_revenue` is CASH credit only — pipeline value is never folded in — and is computed under the profile's configured attribution model.

Sorting is server-side (`sort`), and pagination is cursor-based: read `pagination.cursor` and pass it back as `?cursor=`. The token is opaque; its contents are not part of the contract.

get.summary: Get one organic post's AI analysis and twin ads
get.description:
The stored AI read on a post — score, fatigue, hook/CTA/emotional/audience notes, strengths, weaknesses, suggestions — plus the paid ads whose creative copy embeds nearest to its caption.

NO DATE RANGE, deliberately. Everything here is a property of the CREATIVE: the analysis is one row written by a background pass, and the twin ads carry lifetime spend and lifetime credited revenue. Nothing moves when the caller changes the window, so accepting `date_from`/`date_to` and ignoring them would be worse than not accepting them. For windowed credit, use `GET /api/v1/organic/posts/{id}`.

READ-ONLY: this route serves what the metered background pass already wrote and never runs a model.

`{id}` is the platform's own post id — the `post_id` on each row of `GET /api/v1/organic/posts`. A post id belonging to another profile answers 404, never 403. A post the pass has not reached answers 200 with `analysis: null`.

Credit for a single story: its insights row, headline KPIs, the customers it holds credit for, and the story replies Atribu matched to a touch.

`{id}` is the story's `ig_media_id`. A story id belonging to another profile answers 404, never 403.

`customers` and `replies` are customer identity and require `customers:read` ON TOP of `analytics:read`; without it both are null and the rest of the response is unchanged.
